> > >Wes, as to my understanding (brought to me by French scientist Mr. 
>Fourier)
> > >ALL
> > >sound waves are a mixture of sine waves (and their phase shifted 
>buddies
> > >called
> > >cosines). Any transients appearing in a low tone momentarily add 
>additional
> > >sinewaves to the tone. These transients can be a multiple of the
> > >fundamental
> > >(overtones) or if they are not an overtone then they potentially 
>interfere
> > >with
> > >the lower tone which is sometimes called intermodulation. 
>Intermodulation
> > >becomes possible in a non linear environment at the source of the tones 
>or
> > >inside the pickup unit (microphone or ear). Intermodulation produces 
>new
> > >frequencies. If two tones of 1kHz and 90Hz would start to intermodulate 
>in
> > >a non
> > >linear fashion inside the ear (in case the 90 Hz is a loud tone f.e.) 
>then
> > >the
> > >additional new frequencies you'd hear are 900 Hz and 1100Hz. These new
> > >frequencies are not externally measurable unless intermodulation 
>already
> > >takes
> > >place at the sound source (like in an overdriven speaker membrane where 
>the
> > >high
> > >bass amplitudes intermodulate with lower amplitude high frequency 
>tones).
> > >This out of the way, back to our hum problem. We are concerned with low
> > >energy
> > >low frequency tones (or noise). If these tones were intermodulation
> > >products of
> > >other tones then it is apparent that these are the higher frequency 
>product
> > >of
> > >the intermodulation (like the 1100Hz in the example above). In my case 
>the
> > >higher frequency of this (for this matter intermodulation product) is
> > >around
> > >71.5 Hz. So if there were any infrasonic sound generating 
>intermodulation
> > >products then one of the original (real) frequency components would be
> > >somewhere
> > >below 20 Hz. Say at 10 Hz. Then the other original (real) frequency in 
>the
> > >equation would need to be at 81.5 Hz. Intermodulation of 10 Hz and 81.5
> > >gives
> > >the new (audible but unmeasurable if intermodulation takes place in the 
>ear
> > >only) frequencies of 71.5 Hz and 91.5 Hz.
> > >Now I am asking you: why do I hear the 71.5 Hz and not the 91.5 and not 
>the
> > >external (loud) 81.5 Hz, why don't microphones pick up the 81.5 Hz nor 
>the
> > >10 Hz
> > >or any other loud tones in this range which could be part of the 
>equation?
> > >The answer is simple: because the hum is not an acoustic 
>intermodulation
> > >product.
> > >
> > >And now to your repeated mentioning of pulses and transients.
> > >Pulses (I assume these are sharp rises of air pressure?) and transients 
>(I
> > >assume these are fast events?) always create a long trail of harmonics 
>in
> > >connection with sound. These long trails of harmonics carry over into 
>the
> > >better
> > >audible range. If my hum would be accompanied by pulses or transients 
>then
> > >these
> > >would be heard much louder than the steady low rumble of the hum.
> > >If the pulses and transients are brought into the context with 
>infrasonic
> > >sound
> > >(everything is relative) then there would be a trail of harmonics 
>rising up
> > >from
> > >the infrasonic range. F.e. if there would be transients happening 
>around 8
> > >Hz
> > >then there would be at least a harmonic at 24, 40, 56, 72.....Hz. 
>Weaker
> > >overtones could also be observed at the even multiples of the 
>fundamental
> > >of 8
> > >Hz. Why then is it that I only hear a 0.5 to a few Hz amplitude 
>modulated
> > >71.5
> > >Hz tone and nothing else?
> > >The answer is simple: because there are no transients happening at 8 Hz 
>or
> > >thereabout.
> > >
> > >BTW I did extensive measurements in the infrasonic range with an 
>electret
> > >microphone inside my house. The amount of airpressure fluctuations as
> > >picked up
> > >by the microphone, caused by the slightest breeze outside the house is
> > >tremendous. These fluctuations cause sound waves with a frequency up to 
>10
> > >Hz
> > >with amplitudes 100 times higher than say my fridge compressor at 48 Hz
> > >measured
> > >from a distance of one metre.
> > >Within a metre listening distance from the fridge I can just barely 
>hear
> > >the
> > >fundamental of 48 Hz because it gets drowned out by its harmonics, but 
>I
> > >never
> > >managed to hear the infrasonic waves created by winds of ANY
> > >strength.........
> > >
> > >Please note that the sound energy arriving at the eardrum required to 
>hear
> > >something at 20 Hz needs to be about 100 million times higher compared 
>to
> > >the
> > >energy required at 3.5 kHz.
> > >So if we are talking about hearing low frequency acoustic waves, we are 
>not
> > >talking about chickenfeed, there is quite a bit of energy in audible
> > >soundwaves
> > >in this low frequency range hence relatively easy picked up by electret
> > >microphones (which do not have the significant sensitivity rolloff of 
>the
> > >human
> > >ear which starts at about 700 Hz).

Hi Peter, I will try you recommendation some time and let you know. But the 
reason I am writing this response, is that my location here in Washington 
state, the NLK site at Jim Creek, offers something very different. Last 
year, after I noticed that I could here the tones and first became aware of 
them, I continued to listen.It was while I was in bed and trying to go to 
sleep, that I first became aware of the tones. So about 6 to 10 months 
later,I purchased an entirely new bed and mattress set. The point being, it 
was a little higher off the floor and had more stuffings, you know, and I 
noticed it sort of muffled the tones. I was surprised, but accepted it with 
pure logic, that I was hearing something from outside my head, and with the 
new bed set, the tones were muffled!!! I still hear them to this day, but 
with a modified acceptance, compared with the first time I became aware.In 
other words, I hear the tones and there are times when they are guieter than 
normal, and times when they are very loud and strong. The same comparison 
applies at times when I am traveling close to the Towers, or if I am further 
away on the back-roads, rural settings.  Rick

I concure with Dorothy, the tones are always the same for me too. The only 
thing that changes, is the duration of either tone,or just one of them. 
Usually the low tone is the longer one in duration and usually the higher 
tone is the shorter one. But under all circumstances, the 2 tones are always 
the same note, different from each other but never changing.When I first 
became aware of the tones, I first heard the low one with a "space" in 
between the next low tone. But within a few days or so, I really understood 
that there was a higher tone as well. Since that realization, they have been 
characteristically stable under all circumstances, even though I can change 
my surrounding factors (day noise, location outside, location within my 
house ,in my car,etc).Rick

>USGS/Stanford University geophysicist A. C. Fraser-Smith
>(http://www-star.stanford.edu/~acfs/fraser-smith-research.html) has
>discovered a possible relation between ULF (ultra low frequency signals in
>the Earth) and earthquakes:
>
>Fraser-Smith, A. C., A. Bernardi, P. R. McGill, M. E. Ladd, R. A. 
>Helliwell,
>and O. G. Villard, Jr., "Low-Frequency Magnetic Field Measurements near the
>Epicenter of the Ms 7.1 Loma Prieta Earthquake," Geophys. Res. Letters,
>17,1465-1468, 1990.
>
>Put that together with the following: Dr. Michael Persinger has discovered
>that global geomagnetic disturbances (ULF signals) have a direct effect on
>the brain because and -- get this -- on vestibular balance, which is 
>related
>closely to anomalies in the inner ear. Based on my electrosmog stress
>hypothesis, I postulate that some people may experience the hum as a result
>of this additional ULF-caused stress.
>
>As he explained it me
>(http://www.sonic.net/~west/mc/persinger.htm):
>
>"We suspect that significant bioeffects can be evoked with even smaller
>intensities if they are applied for longer periods of time. For example, we
>found that odd vestibular experiences increase within our experimental
>setting if there has been a global geomagnetic disturbance of more than 25
>nT the night before and the global geomagnetic activity is still above 25
>nT. Our experimental work with rats who display enhanced electrical 
>lability
>within the limbic system have shown that only one hour exposure to 7 Hz 
>sine
>waves whose amplitudes incrementally increase and decrease in successive 30
>sec increments between 10 and 50 nT (much like the earth's magnetic field)
>can evoke significantly neuroelectrical discharges."

Thank you, Wes, for the links which I will read with interest after I
get off work.  I was already familiar with the findings of Fraser-Smith
which were discovered during Loma Prieta. I did not know about the
findings of Dr. Persinger. I had a personal interest in the Loma Prieta
as it leveled the Cypress structure only a mile or so from where I
worked, and completely terrorized my daughter who worked for the same
company. Our hope, of course, is that somehow these things can someday
be reliably predicted. So, I read Fraser-Smith's reports with high
interest.

The only one I ever hit exactly was the M7+ Hector Mine, a year or two
ago; my first alert was an incredibly long hum attenuation which lasted
more than a day (attenuations usually are minutes to hours), documented
later to be accompanied by the occurrence of an X-Class (if I remember
correctly) flare with associated CME, followed closely by a suspicious
swarm (foreshocks) in the Hector Mine area, which allowed me to pinpoint
the location as well as the timing. I thought at the time that the
magnitude might be related to the duration of the attenuation, but have
no idea if that is true. But that really presents a lot of variables,
and if any of them are missing, prediction is not possible by that
method. As you know, giant quakes often occur unheralded by noteworthy
foreshocks and many are completely unassociated with flaring, so fine
tuning a theory becomes a venture in frustration because geologic time
moves so slowly.

Incidentally, the little swarm at Coso Junction you all were discussing
here were foreshocks of a M4.9 (which actually itself could be a
foreshock, although I hope not) which occurred there yesterday.

Best regards,

Judy

Judy,

Don't overdose on that iron in the coffee water!

Your area sounds very much like mine, the iron, quartz.
We are probably great receiving antennas.

Three years or so ago we had an earthquake just to the west of me.  I think
it was like a 3.5  or so on the scale.  It was considered pretty strong for
this area.  I had been hearing the hum for weeks without let up and at 6:00
p.m. the eveing before the quake the hum stopped suddenly.  At sometime
after 8:00 a.m. the quake happened.  The hum returned the next day after the
quake.  I remembering recording this, as I too wandered if the quake might
have had anything to do with the hum stopping so suddenly.

It is 107 degrees outside just now, so I don't think it will be so hot out
your way. at least I hope not.


Anne

> Hi all,
>
> I'd like to invite you to do a simple experiment - absolutely no equipment
is
> necessary.
>
> What you need:
> some environmental noise around you (computer fan, birds, refrigerator
running,
> stereo, spouse/kids rummaging about, toilet cistern filling noise, etc.)
and
> THE HUM.
>
> Now you hold tight your nose and mouth and try to breathe in with moderate
> strength. At the same time you swallow. It will make one or two bangs the
> moment your middle ears get evacuated and your eardrums form a concave
> depression caused by the low pressure inside your ears.
> The pre tensioned eardrums will be picking up somewhat less noise from
around
> you as you can easily tell.
>
> The question is: does the volume of your hum change during this
experiment?
>
> Please let me know the results of your experiments.
>
> cheers, Peter.
>

Wes,

Thanks for these good sites.  It was good to read the one on Dr.
Pinsingher's studies.  I could sure relate to some of the things he was
discussing .

You seem to be the man to ask this question.  I have not had the hum now
since around June 5th, and it had been very bad before that time.  I decided
to take a VHF/UHF antenna down from over the roof on the south end of my
house.  I have a high pitched roof and it was sitting almost on it.  The
storm had damaged it a little and it seemed like the thing to do during the
bad hum episode.  It had been there for about 6 or more years.  I never had
the hum before it was on there.  I took it down and have not had the hum
since.  I know it could be just a coincidence and I am trying to not get
overly optimistic about it, though I want to.

Anne

I'd like to invite you to do a simple experiment - absolutely no equipment is
necessary.

What you need:
some environmental noise around you (computer fan, birds, refrigerator running,
stereo, spouse/kids rummaging about, toilet cistern filling noise, etc.) and
THE HUM.

Now you hold tight your nose and mouth and try to breathe in with moderate
strength. At the same time you swallow. It will make one or two bangs the
moment your middle ears get evacuated and your eardrums form a concave
depression caused by the low pressure inside your ears.
The pre tensioned eardrums will be picking up somewhat less noise from around
you as you can easily tell.

The question is: does the volume of your hum change during this experiment?

Please let me know the results of your experiments.

> Hej Peter.

> interested in'. Another of Anders' reason for applying a filter is, I believe,
> to reduce his signal bandwidth before signal analysis, which on the
> filtered version still can tie up his computers for several hours. Maybe an
> un-filtered version would double or treble the computer analysis time.
> Better ask Anders for a more complete version of his filter philosophy.

>

> your perceived hum as yet?" No. The reason is that I have been aware of

Stefan,

I think we can pretty much rule out a direct acoustic excitation for being
responsible for our hums.
Unfortunately I cannot comment on tinnitus but maybe it enters our consciousness
through another neuronal path than the hum. If tinnitus were a 100% internal affair
and the hum not, then the two neuronally carried events could be "traveling" along
different roads to the same destination - our consciousness. The one path could
have more exposure to the hearing path hence it is more susceptible to being
influenced by acoustic signals (the path which carries hum can interfere with sound
signals, while the other "tinnitus path" cannot be influenced by externally applied
noise of any color).
The technical term crosstalk springs to mind which, as you might know, is the
(unwanted) ability of electrical signals in wires influencing other signals in
other wires which run parallel to them.

One of  the possible explanations for your delayed sensation of the hum after the
ear slapping could be that the neurons carrying, or the hum sensor itself, needs
more time to recover than your hearing system. Maybe its in the two organs of
balance?
There are some grains of magnetite in everyone's head, maybe these are getting
excited in some people by not unknown but unsuspected external forces?
Just take the geomagnetic field for example. This field changes not only slowly and
steadily, there are "overtones" in its movement - and this in a three dimensional
fashion, and the sense of balance has sensors which can sense three dimensional
events.....
Maybe there is a remainder from a sense in us which early humans in tectonically
unstable environments could profit from, a sense which gave them enough warning
before an earthquake f.e. which would manifest itself in many cases through
geomagnetic anomalies.....
Another example of internally generated noise is shaking the head - in my case this
produces a barely noticeable tone of about 1 kHz while shaking, and after this a
relatively loud hum sensation (around 70 Hz)  for a few minutes. I bet that the
source for the 1 kHz has something to do with the position of my internal hum
sensor. So if someone could tell me, where the 1 kHz comes from then this would be
a good place to look for the hum sensor.

friendly greetings.....Peter.

Inside the SOUND seems to be coming from the chimney stack or nearest 
wall. Outside the SOUND seems to be coming from the steep mountain side 
behind my house. On the other side of Hunneberg, the SOUND still seems to 
be coming from the mountain side. When I'm outside in terrain with no 
prominent vertical features, on flat land, the SOUND usually seems to be 
louder in a certain direction, and usually this direction changes over time.

To me this is consistent with an acoustic vibration in the crust of the 
Earth. Anders' geophone recordings of the Hum is also consistent with this 
interpretation.

If the Hum on the other hand was originating from a transmitter of EM 
radiation, I would expect some directional properties of the Hum 
sensation. If the Hum was an internally produced phantom sound like 
tinnitus, I would expect no directional properties.

Hello Peter, I have a report to make after trying your experiment.When I got 
home, the conditions were about as perfect as I could find..usually it is 
quiet enough to really concentrate on the tones I hear..so for the end of 
the day it was still very quiet, I went into my bedroom and started to 
listen for the tones, to try your experiment. It was 8:45 pm,PST.I plugged 
my nose and tried to inhale with force.A few seconds into this, I started to 
hear pops and crackles, then my right ear popped. I couldnt believe I was 
actually hearing all that noise!!! After about 10 to 15 seconds of trying to 
inhale, I stopped to listen for the effects or the tones. They were almost 
immediately heard again, the same as before the test, although there was 
something different about the way the tones sounded.This evaluation period 
was for about 1 minute or so. Then I tried the process again and within a 
couple of seconds, I heard my left ear crack loudly, along with a few short 
crackling noises, then I stopped to listen for the effects or the tones 
again.As I stood there, my hearing was different, sort of muffled. That was 
my first impression, and as the next few seconds turned into the first 
minute, I was still focused on trying to listen for the tones.Then I 
realized I could not confirm hearing the tones any longer. I continued to 
stand there in complete silence for a total of about 5 minutes and tried 
very hard to convince myself that I could hear the tones, but I could not 
actually verify or confirm that I could hear them. So the experiment did 
have an effect on my hearing. It was then that I noticed the "close" and 
normal noises were actually muffled, and as I shifted some papers around, or 
talked, the sounds were very muffled.The first part of the test caused some 
muffling but I didnt notice it enough to know what to call the effect.But at 
the end of the second part, which popped my left ear, I could confirm the 
total muffling of sound, as perceived within both my ears and head, and 
understood that in the first part of the test it muffled my hearing in the 
right ear only.Now that both ears were muffled by the test I could confirm 
that my hearing was affected in a negative way, which muffled both ears and 
made the close noises sound muffled as well as a slight echo or far away 
effect.I tried to listen for the tones again for a few minutes and I thought 
I could barely hear them but actually could not confirm that. Sometimes the 
tones do sound barely audible, but in this case with the test, I only 
"think" they were there but cant say that I can verifiably confirm that I 
heard them. The induced muffling was effective in reducing or eliminating 
the tones but affected my other close hearing senses as well.I anaylized 
this total effect for the first few minutes, as I said, and the effect 
lingered. I continued with my normal evening activities, drank some water 
within the first 5 to 10 minutes of the test. This did not clear the 
muffling of sound , I was thirsty anyway and wasnt trying to clear my ears 
intentionally.I also then had been lying down, and got up again, without any 
change in the effect upon my hearing. Approximatly 45 minutes later 
(9:30,PST) I went to bed and went to sleep, without any change to the 
lingering effect upon my hearing.When I woke up in the morning my hearing 
was normal.I think this test also made my ears feel as if I had been 
swimming and had gotten alot of water in my ears which stayed trapped there, 
making my eardrums feel sore or acheing, at least thats the impression I 
have this morning.So I am curious now. 1) Tinnitis, or leaning toward that? 
2) RF thermal heating 3)Real time accoustic waves?  How do these theories 
play in the part of how this affected my hearing? Thank you and good luck! 
Rick Stanton

Peter,

Ja, du kan ju snacka svenska zehr gut, aber ...

> sound waves would create. In the frequency range of interest the
> sound waves are
> several metres long, so you should be able to hear their volume
> change by moving
> around your head by several tens of centimetres.

Sound wavelengths that long are not directional and head movements would not
be effective. You can confirm that by listening to a subwoofer. At that
wavelength, sound inside a building is distributed somewhat evenly, with
louder maxima in rooms with dimensions matching its resonant frequency.

A quick test is to construct a tube that is resonant at the perceived
frequency and see if the perceived sound is increased, compared to a tube of
another frequency (do not use harmonic frequencies to avoid picking up
harmonics of the fundamental). The only effective test of directionality is
outdoors in an open area to avoid reflections, as you point out. Hold the
tube up to your ear or to a microphone and record it. Rotate the tube
horizontally in a circle to find the source direction.

What frequency are we talking about here?

Another important test is to determine if the perceived sound is a result of
intermodulation artifacts from (inaudible) infrasound.
http://www.borderlands.com/archives/arch/gavreaus.htm is a good source of
construction details for infrasound sensors (may be dangerous; an infrasound
expert should supervise any construction).

Wes,

I think you have quoted me out of the context slightly.
I meant the soundwaves inside any room would create interference patterns with
their reflections. This can be heard even at low frequencies by moving (not
turning) the head inside the listening room. Of course the sound direction
finding properties of the two ears together only works for the higher range
because this is where the phase differences between the two ears are sufficient
to let the ears determine the wave's direction. Is that clear sir ;)

And now to your infrasound theory:

in order for the infrasound to be felt or sensed it needs to be loud enough.
In order to create an intermodulation there needs to be at least one more
frequency.

Say if two infrasonic frequencies intermodulated in your ears which would
produce the sum of the two original frequs, then the result would be a tone of
max 30Hz. Still, the infrasonic sound would need to be powerful enough to start
an intermodulation in your ears. So powerful that the sound could be picked up
by microphones. And, of course the hum would be heard muffled if the ear drums
were pretensioned. I think that for the majority of hummers, infrasonic waves do
not cause a direct hum sensation. I do not rule out however a long term effect
in which the ear responds to external excitations (infrasound may be a
contributing factor) by internally creating a hum sensation. So far, there was
only one report indicating that the hum was acoustic (vague though). 4 others
reported no change in hum intensity, one said it did not change any noise and
one can't do it for other reasons (I am talking about the inhalation
experiment).

In one of my earlier experiments I was sitting there at night, listening to the
hum and watching soundwaves in real time on my CRO. The sensitivity of the
microphone was good for covering sound events as low as 2 Hz. The sound content
in this low range constantly changes, most notably due to winds outside. I
repeated this experiments several times and at no time I could see any
correlation on the screen to what I heard. At one stage when the hum was not
present, I still was able to see the strong air pressure fluctuations in this
low range on the CRO.

I also listened to the hum at night outside through various lenghts of  100 mm
PVC sewage pipes (new ones of course). No increase or decrease of hum, only a
discoloration of other faint noises.

If you'd like to find out the direction of any sound waves, two sets of sound
pickup units and a dual channel CRO offer the most elegant solution (a setup
which copies the human sense of hearing in a crude but sufficient way).

Finally, I must say that these experiments were done before I found out that my
hum is not a direct hearing sensation by sound waves.


cheers, Peter.

Even if I have a reasonably good Reevox A77 tape recorder and a pair of 
condensator microphones fed with 50V, I have not even _tried_ to record 
the Hum. The reason is that I met Anders soon after I joined the Taoshum-L 
and immediately found out that he is both better equipped and educated for 
this particular line of work. In spite of being a licensed ham (SM6GXI), also 
with an education as radio officer for the merchant navy in my distant, 
foggy past, I'm extremely lazy at the test bench. This is to say that I know 
enough to be profoundly impressed by Anders' measurement rig and 
procedure.

The reason why Anders' data analyses usually takes several hours to 
perform, and also why he squeezes his data set through a band pass filter, 
is that he has done extensive triangulation experiments, x, y and z, for 
data from two clusters of four geophones separated by abt. 200m (of 
_heavy_ coax cable). For a 8h recording that's a whole lotta data points to 
calculate... His recording equipment weights abt. 100kg and has to be 
trollied out to the test sites.

In short, Anders has already done a lot more in Hum recording than "rick 
stanton" can presently only _dream_ about... His measurement rig has cost 
a substantial amount of money and construction time and effort. He has 
spent many a damp and cold nights out in the bush on recording sessions. In 
short: what Anders has achieved in Hum recording is beyond comparison 
and peer and still this fact is little recognized at the Taoshum-L. You for 
example seems to have brushed aside his measurement results with a 
shrug, as if they were of no importance, almost as if he was a nitwit 
impostor.

Anders has _not_ been able to substantiate my first hypothesis, that the 
Hum originates from underground constructions activity, like from tunnel 
driving machines of unknown type. The movements of the Hum (pseudo-) 
source which his analyses has shown have been inconclusive, at best like 
"erratic movements of a (pseudo-) source". It's however up to Anders to 
present his findings.

>>At this point I should perhaps inform you that Anders has also 
cooperated with some marine biologists in tracking individual whales in 
the sea by triangulation of their individual sounds with a similar 
measurement rig and setup -- hard and soft -- he uses for Hum recordings. 
This work has been a complete success.<<

To conclude our debate on this theme (we cannot reasonably go on forever, 
especially since we seem not to make any progress...):

what counts to _me_ is that I can beyond doubt recognize the Hum I hear 
(or do you prefer the notation "hear") in Anders' recordings.

Friendly greetings from humming (but now also _sunny_, gotta go tend 
some beans) Hunneberg: $£

>of

>start
>an intermodulation in your ears. So powerful that the sound could be picked 
>up

>drums

- MY WOMEN DONE LEFT ME FOR THE MEN-IN-BLACK DEPARTMENT -

A Bolt From The Blue - And Other High-Strangeness In Hartsville, 
Tennessee

At about 10:45 AM Friday (7/6/01), radio station WJKM and CMR 
(Country 
Music
Radio), with
studios in Hartsville, Tennessee was knocked off the air by a very 
powerful
strange energy blast!
There was a crystal clear blue sky, no clouds or rain.  It was not
lightning!

1.All the radio station's lines were knocked out.
2. Several power transformers were blown several blocks away from the
studios (smoke seen
billowing out of one).
3. All phone lines at the newspaper (The Hartsville Vidette), the 
local 
farm
co-op and all other
phones in this small radius were knocked out!
4. Radio station transmitter lost all MOSFETS and the output - tuning
network.
5. All computers at WJKM lost motherboards, network cards etc.
6. ISDN was knocked out.
7. Most all the equipment Zephyr codec and EAS all knocked out.
THERE WAS NOT A CLOUD IN THE SKY! This was not lightning!

In the back of the radio station were DEAD FRIED BIRDS!  Their wings, 
tails
and feet severely
burned. Station secretary Jennifer and sales manager Steve found a 
small
bird still alive hopping
around with its wings and tail feathers burned off. Many of the birds 
were
still alive but badly
burned.

These are smaller birds. The wingspan is not large enough for them to 
get
fried from getting
across a powerline to ground. This was not just one bird.

Steve (sales manager) told me he heard a loud electrical overload 
sound 
then
the power went out.
He told me he has never heard anything like this ever in his life.  
There
was no blown transformer
near the radio station.  The closest burned transformer was at least 
three
city blocks from the
building.

The editor of the Vidette said she was sitting with her back to the 
window.
She heard a loud
roaring sound like an overload and something came through the window 
and a
flash of light went
through the entire building. The Vidette is next door to the radio 
station.

The Power Company, Tri County Electric and Bell South seem to be at a 
loss
to explain the
situation.  This is not the first time WJKM has had strange power 
surge
problems.  It has been
difficult to keep computers up and running at the Hartsville studios 
and
transmitter site.

We have called the local power company and complained to no avail.  
They
seem to be as puzzled
by the problem as we are.  They have placed monitoring equipment on 
the
lines and have seen
nothing unusual.

Yet in this outage the editor of the Vidette told me she keeps all the
computers in the building
unplugged.  The newspaper publishes once a week so they only plug the
computers into power
once a week. Friday the Editors calculator was plugged into the wall 
outlet
and it was destroyed
by the surge.

These surges are not just coming into the power lines. They are also
entering the radio station
through phone lines and the antenna system. This is evident in blown
telephone equipment.
Sometimes the equipment is not destroyed but the program settings are
scrambled or wiped out.

We have surge protectors plugged into surge protectors.  We keep 
MOV's 
by
the boxfulls.

We have been at a loss to make a determination as to the cause of 
these
surges.The only clue as to
what the cause may be has been suggested by our listeners.

Many of the callers to the radio station seem to think that there is 
some
sort of activity at the old
Hartsville nuclear power plant site. My first trip to the site left 
me 
a bit
cold as the place looks like
an abandoned ghost town. With heaps of things lying around, it looks 
like a
good set for a
futuristic movie.

The nuclear power plant is a site that cost the general public 
millions 
of
dollars that was
supposedly never finished. The construction of the plant came to an 
abrupt
halt some years back
leaving the community devastated. TVA (Federal Government) will tell 
you it
is being used as a
storage area only.  Yet I have calls at the radio station from 
listeners who
claim to hear strange
humming sounds coming from the location.

Listeners have seen strange objects overhead. Listeners have claimed 
to 
see
triangular shaped
craft overhead.  Silent black helicopters at all hours of the night.  
Huge
military C-130's heading in
as if to land or leaving the area nose up as if they have just taken 
off.
There are no visible places
for a C-130 to land or take off.  We have searched the area as well 
as 
we
could.

Listeners from the area have called talking about a strange humming 
sound.
Comments like "you
can feel it"  "It makes the hair stand up on your neck" are common.  
We 
also
hear that you can't
locate the source of the humming it seems to be coming from 
everywhere.

This has been mentioned only by people who live near the nuclear 
power 
plant
site. A rural elderly
listener called my morning show extremely upset.  He told us he had 
lost
several beagle puppies in
the area. A friend of his told him that he thought that he had seen 
the 
pups
in the area near the
cooling tower.  He reported to us in a phone call that he had driven 
his
truck to the area.  He
thought he was hearing the beagles out in the wooded area so he 
climbed 
over
the fence and
started calling to them. He told us he was greeted with an overhead
helicopter and a ground force
of about 30 people. They allegedly escorted him off the property in a 
very
rough and crude
manner. He said they were some kind of police, some in plain 
clothes.  
He
told us they were rude
and threatening.

A listener who is a tech that lives on a hill near the area has had
fluorescent bulbs light in his hand
on various spots on his property. He discovered this by accident but 
has
witnesses to the
phenomenon.  He works with surveillance cameras, thermal imaging and 
a 
lot
of high tech stuff.
He tells us there is operational radar being used at the nuclear site 
at
different times.

A Hartsville resident who's ex-husband worked at the site tells us 
that
there is a reactor there. We
have had several reports of this from different folks in the 
community. 
She
tell us that her husband
was told "don't eat the fish from the river or eat any deer shot in 
the
area"

Our local heating and air conditioning contractor tells about how he 
sees
large shinny new 18
wheel tankers go and come from the nuclear site at 3 in the morning.

A gentleman who is a relative to an owner of a local grocery 
establishment
claims to have seen a
Bigfoot near the nuclear plant.

It is also interesting that according listeners have called in, there 
has
apparently been an increase
in what they are calling fibromyalgia. This is a decease name 
appointed 
to
the unexplainable
severe and disabling pain throughout the entire body over recent 
years, 
as
well as, an increase in
headaches mimicking migraines that are not actual migraines.

At night the entire area has a strange chemical smell to it somewhat 
pungent
like ozone and
chemicals. The radio station transmitter and Hartsville studio is 
located in
the middle of Hartsville
City Park about 5 miles from the nuclear cooling tower. We are in no 
way
accusing the TVA or
the nuclear power plant of causing this problem. We are just 
reporting 
what
listeners and residents
of the community have reported to us.

One thing that we do find strange is this, in the beginning we would 
go 
on
the air and joke about
the nuclear power plant. We did this because of the TVA's vague 
promise 
to
turn a good portion
of the land back to the community for development. This was always 
talked
about but nothing
ever happened.

We placed several calls to TVA. No one ever responded. When we would 
get on
the air and start
airing some of these reports it was always promptly followed by a 
press
release or a public
meeting about the donation of the land back to the county. We were 
told 
not
to talk about it, that
the TVA would get upset.

Whenever we would stop talking about it, then it seemed that you 
would 
hear
nothing about the
land development. We have been off the subject for a good time now. 
Their
latest announcement
is to develop the land in partnership with the local Power Company 
for 
an
industrial power park.

They say this wont happen now for 4 years.  They now claim they must 
do 
a 4
year environmental
study.  What do they need to study?

Was there not a study done in order to build a nuclear facility?  
What 
else
needs to be studied for
a commercial business site?  For you the listener, thank you for 
putting up
with our outage. We
are making repairs as fast as we can. As for the cause, we have no 
idea 
what
this is all about.

We are concerned about the charred and fried birds however.
These birds were found on our property in areas where there are no
powerlines! The Power
Company said the birds got into a power transformer. What 
transformer?  
Our
10 KVA pole peg
behind the radio station?

How would all these birds do that?  After being in or near the 
transformer,
how did they all get to
different locations around the 5 acres of land where there are no 
power
lines? If the birds were
sitting on an electrical wire and were hit by a surge their legs 
would 
have
been burned off!  These
birds have legs. Its their wings and feathers that are burned, singed 
or
missing! It appears to us
these birds were cooked in flight! But by what?

Wes,

I spent about 1 minute at this web site. It's not worth a single second more of
my time.

Any strong transmitter creates high current densities in the earth surrounding
the ground plane of the antenna. Any inhomogenities in the earth influence the
path of these currents. The electrical currents concentrate in layers or objects
which offer the least electrical resistance. If there were any metal pipes in
the vicinity of such an antenna then these pipes would carry a substantial
amount of current. Due to current induced magnetic forces the metal would start
to transfer part of the electrical energy (in case of an amplitude modulated
carrier) into kinetic energy (vibration). This vibration travels through the
rigid pipe work and may be heard at resonating kitchen sinks f.e. (but only if
the modulation/vibration contained audible frequencies and the transmitter were
sending in AM mode).
cheers, Peter.

Hi,

a little while ago I came across interesting scientific research data about
biomagnetic field measurements.
According to this particular report there is a significant frequency (35 Hz)
emanating from the somatosensory area in the brain. Another significant
frequency of 15 Hz can be detected at the auditory area.
External frequencies in this range would most certainly interfere with these
internally generated frequencies if they would enter these areas of the brain I
guess.
In the US, sources for 15 Hz vibrational and sound energy can be found around
heavy electrical machinery (subharmonic of the 60 Hz mains). Could this be an
indication for the fact that there are so many more people complaining about hum
in the US than in Europe where the mains frequency is only 50 Hz?
There are also many (worldwide) sources for EM waves containing this frequency.
The pathway into these areas of the brain could be via the sensory system or via
direct magnetic coupling.
http://www.hut.fi/u/watson/pdf/BM2000abst-207-219.pdf
cheers, Peter.

>I'm puzzled what list members mean by "the" hum. What leads you to think

>characteristics -- are connected? If there are multiple causes (and that

>thinking? And can someone state precisely what the "Taos hum" is and 
>how it differs from the various reports on this list? Or is this a catch-all 
>(and therefore confusing and perhaps meaningless) phrase?

"And can someone state precisely what the "Taos hum" is and how it 
differs from the various reports on this list?" If I went to Taos, NM, _my_ 
hum would automagically be transformed to the Taos Hum. This 
transformation also works the other way around. If you could hear the Hum 
in Taos, you could travel away from Taos while listening to this 
transformation, how the Taos Hum transforms into the Amarillo Hum and 
so on. There is a man who lives only a couple of kilometers from Hunneberg 
and who can also hear a hum and which he describes in similar terms as I 
describe my  hum. He has traveled all over Sweden and has heard his hum 
from north to  south. I have heard my hum everywhere I went in southern 
Sweden, in  Denmark and in the Netherlands. Judy (on the taoshum-l) has 
traveled  extensively in USA and has heard her hum in most places. To you, 
who has  never heard the Hum, this might seem as evidence that we all 
suffer from hallucinations and that the only thing we share is a disease. 
That's OK with me.

Wes, since you're a Scientist who does not hear the Hum, it's only 
_natural_ that you doubt that there is a thing like "the Hum" and that such 
a hypothetical thing could or should have an explanation. This is really 
nothing to worry about. It will all go away when you have realized that 
there is no career to be made from explaining or explaining away of 
anybodys hum.

>From my point of view, there seems to "always" be a Scientist on the 
taoshum-l who assumes the role of explaining to me that I suffer from 
"hearing" phantom sounds, a disease which can only be cured by turning on 
a fan or white noise generator in my bedroom. Now all those Scientists 
have merged into one meta-character in a  play of more or less divine 
archetypes, like Divina Comedia. Then I can only repeat myself: I _believe_ 
my neighbour can hear the same Hum as I, but I cannot _prove_ even what I 
can hear.

Isn't it remarkable that no Scientist can explain how the sense of seeing 
actually works, but that a meeter reading that a Scientist has made by 
using his own eyes still is considered to be "objective" data?

>I think you have quoted me out of the context slightly.
>I meant the soundwaves inside any room would create interference patterns 
>with
>their reflections. This can be heard even at low frequencies by moving (not
>turning) the head inside the listening room. Of course the sound direction
>finding properties of the two ears together only works for the higher range
>because this is where the phase differences between the two ears are 
>sufficient
>to let the ears determine the wave's direction. Is that clear sir ;)
>
>And now to your infrasound theory:
>
>in order for the infrasound to be felt or sensed it needs to be loud 
>enough.
>In order to create an intermodulation there needs to be at least one more
>frequency.
>
>Say if two infrasonic frequencies intermodulated in your ears which would
>produce the sum of the two original frequs, then the result would be a tone 
>of
>max 30Hz. Still, the infrasonic sound would need to be powerful enough to 
>start
>an intermodulation in your ears. So powerful that the sound could be picked 
>up
>by microphones. And, of course the hum would be heard muffled if the ear 
>drums
>were pretensioned. I think that for the majority of hummers, infrasonic 
>waves do
>not cause a direct hum sensation. I do not rule out however a long term 
>effect
>in which the ear responds to external excitations (infrasound may be a
>contributing factor) by internally creating a hum sensation. So far, there 
>was
>only one report indicating that the hum was acoustic (vague though). 4 
>others
>reported no change in hum intensity, one said it did not change any noise 
>and
>one can't do it for other reasons (I am talking about the inhalation
>experiment).
>
>In one of my earlier experiments I was sitting there at night, listening to 
>the
>hum and watching soundwaves in real time on my CRO. The sensitivity of the
>microphone was good for covering sound events as low as 2 Hz. The sound 
>content
>in this low range constantly changes, most notably due to winds outside. I
>repeated this experiments several times and at no time I could see any
>correlation on the screen to what I heard. At one stage when the hum was 
>not
>present, I still was able to see the strong air pressure fluctuations in 
>this
>low range on the CRO.
>
>I also listened to the hum at night outside through various lenghts of  100 
>mm
>PVC sewage pipes (new ones of course). No increase or decrease of hum, only 
>a
>discoloration of other faint noises.
>
>If you'd like to find out the direction of any sound waves, two sets of 
>sound
>pickup units and a dual channel CRO offer the most elegant solution (a 
>setup
>which copies the human sense of hearing in a crude but sufficient way).
>
>Finally, I must say that these experiments were done before I found out 
>that my

> > > around your head by several tens of centimetres.
> >
> > Sound wavelengths that long are not directional and head movements would 
>not
> > be effective. You can confirm that by listening to a subwoofer. At that
> > wavelength, sound inside a building is distributed somewhat evenly, with
> > louder maxima in rooms with dimensions matching its resonant frequency.
> >
> > A quick test is to construct a tube that is resonant at the perceived
> > frequency and see if the perceived sound is increased, compared to a 
>tube of
> > another frequency (do not use harmonic frequencies to avoid picking up
> > harmonics of the fundamental). The only effective test of directionality 
>is
> > outdoors in an open area to avoid reflections, as you point out. Hold 
>the
> > tube up to your ear or to a microphone and record it. Rotate the tube
> > horizontally in a circle to find the source direction.
> >
> > What frequency are we talking about here?
> >
> > Another important test is to determine if the perceived sound is a 
>result of
> > intermodulation artifacts from (inaudible) infrasound.
> > http://www.borderlands.com/archives/arch/gavreaus.htm is a good source 
>of
> > construction details for infrasound sensors (may be dangerous; an 
>infrasound
> > expert should supervise any construction).
>

Hi gang,

I was recently watching late night tv, one of those unsolved mysteries
programs when they showed a piece on the "Taos Hum".  Having heard a "hum"
since the early 80's and having been completly dissmissed by doctors and
friends over the issue, I was thrilled to find there were others that
appeared to hear some thing very similar to what I was hearing. Knowing that
you can find almost anything on the web and now for the first time having a
name, I went searching and found all of you.

It's the "Taos Hum" because a large enough group of apparently credible
people kept pushing until some one took notice.  It wasn't a single person
that could be dismissed and they weren't a group of "loonies" that could be
dismissed.  They were a group of people that non "hummers" just couldn't
ignor, there were too many of them and they just weren't the type that would
make something like this up.  Thus, the "Taos Hum".

I think it's "the" hum because  if you are amongst those that can't hear it
and are foolish enough to mention it, you will get a pat on the back and
some condesending comment.  It's the reaction to our discussing it, not "it"
that makes it "the" hum.  My Medford, Oregon hum may be the same as the Taos
hum, I don't know.

When I first heard it some 20 years ago, the hum was very irritating.  There
is some thing about not being able to identify an object that will cause it
to become an obsession.  You do get to the point however that you can push
it to the back most of the time.  Right now, surrounded by fans,electrical
noise and cars going by on the street outside I have to stop and search for
it.  It's there, but I have to search.  At night when the ambient noise is
low I can't escape it, it won't go away.

There have been two occassions in the last 20 years when there was an
absense of hum that I could not account for.  Once was in the wilderness and
once was in the middle of a big city.  Weird, huh.  I have stedfastly
believed that the noise was from outside me.  However, there have been two
incidents in recent years that have caused me to consider the part played by
substances we ingest.

If we take a substance and the hum either goes away or becomes louder, does
that suggest that the substance is capable of enhancing or reducing our
abilities to hear what is outside us or that the sound is generated from
inside us rather than outside us.

A few years ago after the breakup of my marriage, I agreed to take Prozac
for depression.  I remained on it for 3 months, then said thanks but no
thanks.  The ONLY benifit I got from the Prozac was that the hum completly
dissapeared.  It was gone, completly, totaly gone.  It was almost worth the
price to stay on it to keep the hum gone.  After 15 years of hum, the quiet
was soooo wonderful.  With in 36 hours of stopping the Prozac, the hum was
back.

Okay, incident two.  Six months ago, irritated by my inability to
concentrate I ordered one of those dumb supplements off the television.
Focus Factor was it's name.  "Nutritional support for enhanced mental
concentration" the bottle claims.  Well, my hum became so loud that it
couldn't be pushed into the background any longer.This was the first and
only time that the hum did not feel like it came completly from outside, it
completly surrounded me, feeling as though it were both inside and outside
of me.  With in 36 hours of stopping the Focus Factor, the hum was back to
normal.

So, some would argue that this is proof that the hum is not real, but rather
generated by my brain.  I might on the other hand argue that these
substances either subdue or enhance my ability to hear sounds.  The truth
is, I don't have a clue.  The hum is there, it's been there for 20 years and
my impression has almost always been that it is from outside me.

What is the old joke, just because your paranoid doesn't mean they aren't
out to get you?

Well, hope you all have a good day.     Cathy

Hi Rick,

sorry I cannot give you a direct answer to your questions. There are just too
many possible factors which potentially let you hear the modulation content of
an AM carrier inside a house.
Theoretically a lot depends on the distance between the vibration prone water
pipes and the ground plane of such an antenna. Once the pipe work starts to
vibrate (at the closest distance to the antenna) then I could imagine that this
kind of vibration could be made audible by resonators located several miles
away.
Perhaps Anders could give you a better idea about the acoustic conductivity of
water pipes since apparently he currently is into studying hum conducted through
these pipes.

Now to your other question whether or not you were experiencing an infrasonic
sound wave when in close proximity to NLK.
Possible sources for sound/vibration in the infrasonic or close to it, are
vibrations through the earth caused by the electricity generating equipment.
Another source would be the magnetically induced mechanical vibrations of the
antenna wires which then get coupled into the earth through the poles. A
condition for infrasonics to be conducted away from the transmitter of course is
that the modulation content needs to have infrasonic frequencies in it which is
quite likely (unless they used their naval facilities solely to transmit music
to keep up these lonely sailors' spirits ;)

cheers, Peter.

Peter,

I have considered this.  When I was about 4  years old, I climbed up on the
bathroom sink and ate an entire bottle of orange flavored asprin (early
1950's).  My parents found me unconsious and got me to the hospital barely
in time to save my life.  The only thing I remember from the experience was
the lound scream or hum in my head.  That noise was different from the hum
that I have heard the last twenty years, though similar to some of the sound
I experienced from the Focus Factor.

One of the reason that I have steadfastly believed the hum to be outside is
some hearing tests I had done in the early 80's.  When I was done, the
doctor just shook his head and said that I could be used to calibrate the
machine, my hearing was so acute at the lower range.  When I discussed the
"hum" with him, he felt that I was truly hearing something, but he didn't
know what.

I might add that I also have a very acute sense of smell.  I can smell food
going bad 1 or 2 days before any one else can detect anything, used to drive
my mother nuts.  I often smell things that no one else can.  Some times I
can identify it, other time I don't have a clue.  Not sure if the two are
related, but the reaction to these two "talents" is about the same, a pat on
the back and a roll of their eyes.  Do other "hummers" also have an acute
sense of smell?

Cathy

"I might on the other hand argue that these substances either subdue or 
enhance my ability to hear sounds". This is my impression too. I have 
thoroughly tested almost every psychoactive substance there is on planet 
Earth. Smoking cannabis for example tends to enhance sounds which are 
normally suppressed under your awareness threshold. Under the influence 
of cannabis, the Hum is consequently perceived to be louder and more 
annoying. Substances which raise your serotonine level, either by MAO 
inhibition like Prozac or for example yohimbine (from African Yohimbe 
bark, not yet a controlled substance, hi-hi) or by mimicking serotonine in 
your matabolism (which natural substance does this trick the best I will 
not reveal since it is little known and hence not yet illegal) tend to lock 
you into a cocoon of increased mental activity. This will of course make 
external stimuli seem less important in your field of awareness and 
consequently the Hum is pushed into the background. This is by the way the 
'normal' state of mind of most people.

> -----Original Message-----
> From: Stefan Lofstrand [mailto:hunneberg@telia.com] said:

> it's only _natural_ that you doubt that there is a thing like "the Hum"
and
> that such a hypothetical thing could or should have an explanation.

I didn't make myself clear. I have no reason to doubt the objective (or
subjective) existence of any reported "hum" phenomena, especially since
there is no experimental data supporting that conclusion. I was simply
asking what was the logic that has persuaded some people on the list to
definitively ascribe all reported experiences on the list to a _single_
cause ("the" hum), given the fact that the reported experiences on the list
vary so widely and given the fact that no one has presented (to my
knowledge; I may have missed it) any scientific research to support such an
single-cause hypothesis.

In other words, what is the evidence that there is a single cause? Rick, for
example, reports two tones that intensify when he approaches the Navy
transmitter, which strongly implies that he is experiencing a local (rather
than a worldwide) phenomenon, perhaps causes by "RF hearing" or infrasound
from geneators. Others sense the hum independently of their location, which
implies a cause that is very different, perhaps a harmonic of a pervasive
infrasound or perhaps an endogenous cochlear "fill-in" compensation. What
leads list members to think there is only one explanation and what exactly
is that explanation?

> taoshum-l who assumes the role of explaining to me that I suffer from
> "hearing" phantom sounds

I'm not asserting any explanation for the mechanism of your hearing. That
would be foolish in the absence of any laboratory results and expert
analysis.

Hi Kathleen, how are you? I was wondering how you determined the hum had 2 
tones?What do they sound like to you? For me, they are the same 2 tones, 
shifting between them from high to low, but sustaining each note for a 
second or a few seconds.They appear to be about 1 or 2 octaves between the 
two, I need to do further studies and get some equipment to be able to 
monitor the musical aspect,etc. They are musical in that sense and are 
always the same 2 tones. It is for this reason that I call it "Tones" 
instead of a hum. I have observed that by the description of others, the hum 
to them, might actually be the lower portion of the same, or similar, 2 
tones. The idleing or diesel effect are what I compare to being equivelant 
to the lower tone, whereas airplane propellar noise from a distance, is 
compared to the high tone.I call this the "family" of noises,used only as a 
comparison for myself and for others, to be able to describe the kind of 
noises that they hear.I dont know if it has helped but its nice to know that 
a few others are able to describe the noise as being a series of Tones.Based 
on what I hear up here, along with the descriptions given by others, I think 
its possible they might be hearing only the lower portion of the same noise, 
therefor they call it a "hum". I would tend to agree with them about it 
being a hum if I only focused on the lower tone. But within a few days of my 
initial discovery of the noise, I realized it was actually 2 tones. 
Aparently I am the only one here in Washington state who hears these things 
as a tone. One other person lives further up north and describes his 
experiance as being more of a bothersome "rumble". My guess would be that 
this could be only the lower portion of the same noises I hear, yet somehow 
magnified because of the greater distance. I travel near these Towers 
occationally ( this is a very large and powerful Navy transmitting site)Take 
care. Rick

>I didn't make myself clear. I have no reason to doubt the objective (or
>subjective) existence of any reported "hum" phenomena, especially since
>there is no experimental data supporting that conclusion. I was simply
>asking what was the logic that has persuaded some people on the list to
>definitively ascribe all reported experiences on the list to a _single_
>cause ("the" hum), given the fact that the reported experiences on the list
>vary so widely and given the fact that no one has presented (to my
>knowledge; I may have missed it) any scientific research to support such an
>single-cause hypothesis.
>
>In other words, what is the evidence that there is a single cause? Rick, 
>for
>example, reports two tones that intensify when he approaches the Navy
>transmitter, which strongly implies that he is experiencing a local (rather
>than a worldwide) phenomenon, perhaps causes by "RF hearing" or infrasound
>from geneators. Others sense the hum independently of their location, which
>implies a cause that is very different, perhaps a harmonic of a pervasive
>infrasound or perhaps an endogenous cochlear "fill-in" compensation. What
>leads list members to think there is only one explanation and what exactly
>is that explanation?
>
> > taoshum-l who assumes the role of explaining to me that I suffer from

  Information from another source that may be of assistance to some,

 << Re: the question of photonics.  Let me try to explain some rather
  difficult concepts, that may help.  This is necessarily an
  oversimplification, but it is a quick rehash of an article I once wrote
  and didn't ever sell.  
  
  Some of this nuclear physics stuff is also counter-intuitive, and needs
  to be just accepted on face value unless you are prepared to spend years
  in learning about quantum physics and the dozens of particles that make
  up atoms.
  
                                         ----------
  
  Photons are seen as particles which have varying amounts of energy,
  depending on the frequency of the photon.  That doesn't make much sense
  to most people, but the physicists believe that light and radio waves
  exist in a dual state which can be viewed sometimes as a particle (a
  bullet) and sometimes as a wave (they call it a 'waveicle').  The
  difference being that a particle exists in a finite piece of space,
  while a wave is spread over a wide front.  In basic physics theory,
  there is a paradox, which is explained away by saying the photon is
  both.  You can treat it as either ... or both.
  
  So a photon is the basic "atom" of light and radio.  And it is part of a
  group of sub-atomic particles called bosons.  Bosons are uncharged
  particles, and therefore photon beams can pass through each other, or
  through any transparent medium without one photon influencing the other. 
  
  Light photons which exist at high energy levels and higher frequencies,
  can pass through transparent media only, like glass and water and air.
  
  Radio waves at lower energy levels (per photon) and lower frequencies,
  will pass a certain distance through body tissue.  This is because of
  the frequency and the size of the tissue molecules.
  
  Electrons (which make up electric currents) and the larger ions (which
  make chemicals reactive) canÃ¢â‚¬â„¢t readily do this because they are
  electrically charged, and therefore potentially biologically active to
  the cells immediately surrounding them.  They need to produce chain
  effects in a succession of molecules, for their effects to travel over
  greater distances than one molecule of separation.  
  
  Electrons and ions both create electro-magnetic fields around them, and
  in turn, they are influenced by external electro-magnetic fields.  One
  field needs to interact with another in order for anything to happen -
  just as a compass needs to have its own N-S magnetic field in order to
  point to the North using the earth's magnetic field.  Or the electrons
  from the +ve side of a battery need to flow to the -ve side of the
  battery.  Neither the compass or the +ve pole of a battery will react at
  all with something having no fields or electrical potential.
  
  Photons don't have any electrical charge and therefore you can't measure
  any electrical or magnetic field around a light wave, and nor can you
  effect a light wave by surrounding it with an electical or magnetic field.
  
  So photons are entirely neutral in terms of the fields.  But each photon
  contains a certain fixed amount of energy, dependent on the frequency of
  the photon. Phyicists can calculate this energy level to about twenty
  decimal places. Radio has the least, microwaves have more, light has
  more still, ultraviolet even more, then X-rays and gamma rays have the
  most.  But apart from the frequency differences (and therefore the
  energy differences), all photons are the same.
  
  All that a photon can do (as currently understood) at the lower
  radio/light end of the scale is to be absorbed, and therefore give up
  its energy to the particle which absorbs it.  The photon then
  disappears, since it is nothing more than encapsulated energy.  That
  makes the electrons in the molecule spin more, and they in turn pass on
  their new "heat" energy to surrounding molecules.
  
  One of the big remaining arguments here, is whether the energy from the
  photon transfers to a molecule and emerges instantly as heat (thermal
  effects) -- or whether something else takes place between the absorption
  and the emission of heat (athermal effects).  
  
  We know that eventually all energy emerges as heat, but it is possible
  that there are interim stages that cause changes/damage to biological
  cells in the process.
  
  At the high end of the  EMF continuum (radio--microwave--light--x-ray),
  just above the blue colour in visible light, the photons have enough
  energy when absorbed by a cell molecule to agitate the bonds which hold
  some tissue molecules together, and so cause these bonds (called
  'co-valent bonds') to break. Any molecule using carbon, hydrogen and
  oxygen atoms in its makeup will have some of these strong covalent bonds.
  
  Breaking covalent bonds then creates 'ions' -- which are
  "half-molecules" which have strong positive and negative electric
  charges, and therefore seek out other molecules or ions and take over. 
  This is how biological damage occurs.  
  
  So at this level of energy (and above) the photons are believed to be
  'ionising' and the EMF is known as ionising radiation.  This includes
  ultraviolet light, x-rays and gamma rays, all of which are known to
  damage DNA and cause cancer.
  
  The "Thermal-only" theorists believe that any photon below this
  frequency (light, radio and microwave) can't cause health problems
  because the photons don't have enought energy to break these covalent
  bonds in biological cells, and therefore they can't create adverse
  biological effects.
  
  This, in my opinion, oversimplifies the matter to a ridiculous degree. 
  It may be correct for a photon of light or radio directly impacting on
  the DNA strand in a cell -- but it ignores the potential of a number of
  obvious (and maybe more unknown) mechanisms:
  
  a) Trigger effects (where the cell already has substantial energy
  stored).  This is how we see things with our retinal cells.  The
  biological molecule called photopsin in our eyes is triggered to change
  from one inactive physical state (shape) to another physical state
  (quite different and biologically active) by the absorption of one
  photon of light.  If it didn't, we couldn't see.  
  
  But there is no bond-breaking involved.  The two sides of the molecule
  just twist (tortional) to create a new physical conformation Ã¢â‚¬â€ and that
  triggers the electical signals in the nerves.
  
  The brain then receives these electrical signals, and some parts of the
  brain react electrically ("I can see"), while other parts react with
  chemical changes such as controlling the output of chemical messengers
  like melatonin into the blood stream.  Nowhere in this whole complex
  chain of profound biological effects is there any "breakage of covalent
  bonds".  Yet it all happened because of the impact of non-ionising photons.
  
  b) Secondary effects.  For instance, where the photon joins forces with
  free-radical in a cell (which are already ionised), and these jointly
  produce hydrogen peroxide molecules which can migrate into the cell
  nucleus and then attack the DNA.
  
  This is one of the theories about how DNA damage occurs.  The
  free-radicals aren't generally formed inside the cell nucleus, but
  outside in the cell soma -- so whatever mechanism caused DNA breaks, it
  must be long-lasting enough to migrate from outside the nucleus, in. 
  Hydrogen Peroxide molecules appear to be the most likely.
  
  c) Stochastic resonance effects.  These are similar to the trigger
  effects, but they depend on photon energies being adding to active
  molecular energies ("system noise") to lift the total above the "ionic"
  threshold.  Neither energy-level alone is sufficient to cause DNA
  damage, but when working in harmony, the combination can do so. 
  Currently this is nothing more than a theory.
  
  d) The longitudinal strands of DNA are held together by both co-valent
  bonds (the ones that need to be broken to form ions) while the rungs of
  the DNA ladder comprise hydrogen bonds, and these 'rungs' are easier to
  break. 
  
  In the process of cell-dividion, the cell first unzips the rungs of
  hydrogen bonds, and then a synthesis process using enzymes finds and
  joins the protein strands together into new DNA longitudinal strands. 
  During this synthesis processe, the whole cell process is obviously more
  vulnerable to low-level photon energy impacts -- which could well be
  below the "ionising" threshold.
  
  e) There is also the possibility that cumulative photon (or wave)
  effects may cause the long strands of the DNA (which is coiled and is
  also a semi-conductor) to react in some different way, more as if it
  were a mini-radio receiver. So we aren't talking about single photon
  impacts here.  
  
  The fact that DNA is a semi-conductor means that strands (or parts of
  strands) will always have a positive and negative end whenever they lie
  in any alternating magnetic field (not a static magnetic field like that
  of the earth).  
  
  DNA strands break and are repaired constantly, so applying strong
  alternating electrical or magnetic fields to them is not very sensible,
  if they are electro-active at times the emzymes are trying to make
  repairs.  This could explain the seemingly random, cumulative effects
  that cells need to accumulate before they become cancerous.
  
  So it is a mistake to assume that just because photons of radio lack
  "energy to break chemical bonds" (a crude oversimplification at best)
  then are automatically benign.  
  
  However, that doesn't mean that they are necessarily harmful, either.
  
  It is also important to point out that we are hit by billions of photons
  every second of our lives. Sunlight is probably our strongest source and
  that is millions of times more energy-laden than radio signals, even
  from a nearby TV tower.  Only a cellphone handset comes close to the
  same energy (power-density) levels -- measured at the nearest biological 
 cell.
  
  However all living things have evolved to handle light-frequency
  photons, and we don't know enough about the frequency differences to be
  sure about radio-frequency effects are also benign, since the human
  species has only been accumulating exposure to these in large amounts
  over the last fifty years.  
  
  There's a lot we still don't know.
  
  However we do now know enough to ignore the simplistic calculations of
  radio engineers and radiological physicists when they just do very
  simple energy calculations, and then pronounce radio waves as safe. 
  That is arrogance disguised as expertise.
  
  -----
  
  When someone says the world is moving towards phononics, that is
  actually good news for electrosensitive people because it means that the
  carriage of data (including TV programs) will likely move from radio
  waves transmitted from central antenna, to optical fibres carrying light
  photons, running down each street.  
  
  The fibre acts as a pipe, and the whole purpose of the fibre is to keep
  the light beams (from lasers) within the pipe until it reaches its
  destination. Because light photons don't have any electrical charge,
  they don't have any electrical fields or magnetic fields.
  
  Currently the optical fibre photon beams must be converted back to
  electrical forms in order to be switched, but the next generation of
  telecommunications equipment will be entirely photonic, with switching
  and amplification of the photons without conversion to electricity.
  
  
  --

In quoting something I wrote, I would like to add a small point of 
clarification about my tones up here. As quoted in this letter,it states 
that the tones get louder when I approach the Tower site. Thats not guite 
accurate, for clarification , most of the times that I have approached the 
site, the tones have remained the same in their intensity,as when I was 
farther (several miles) away.Let me put it this way...there have been quite 
a few times when I have heard the Tones very loudly, at home some 15 miles 
away. It is not necessarily a given factor that as I approach them, the 
tones increase. In actuallity, there have been only a couple of  times that 
the tones were very loud and strong at the same time that I was approaching 
them.That just happens to be a random thing about them,whenever they decide 
to operate them at a higher power. They seem to be stable in their chosen 
intensity, between me being near or far. At times when they have been loud, 
I have not been interrested to go for a drive, to approach them to listen to 
them. That would be fun, of course, but I've usually been busy with other 
things or its been during the night, so I dont feel like getting up to go 
for a drive.Its only been a couple of times that I was lucky enough to be 
approaching them while they were at that intense level of operation.The last 
time that happened was about 3 months ago during the day, I took a ride to 
go listen to them and they happened to be broadcasting with an intense 
amount of power. Both tones wer in full force and booming loudly.This was 
the same time that I stepped out of my car and was blasted by the immense 
beam and felt the power force of pressure upon my body.Or maybe it was like 
a magnet drawing me and pulling on me, although there was not actually a 
pulling affect. I've continued to read responses to that report and sort of 
understand that perhaps that effect was caused by some magnetic field or 
grounding effect. But I'll tell you what...the damn things were really 
blasting that day!!!!So, the lesson about this site is that whatever level 
of power they decide to broadcast at, that level is the same, irrespective 
of my proximaty to them.Its been several weeks since I have visited the 
site,and it would be a fun experiment to listen to the level of intensity ( 
either high or low, low seems to be normal)while at home, then go for a 
drive to check and compare the level of intensity once I get there. Plus, at 
other times I have approached them, they have almost been totally inaudible, 
whereas I had to really strain to even "think" that I could hear them!! That 
time I had someone with me and of all times, the things were guiet!!! 
Because of this experiance, I dont believe these tones are caused by some 
sort of Generator equipment.There might be possibly some connection between 
"my approach vs. loudness".If so, then Wes, you may still be correct but at 
this point, I'll have to say the coorelation is not necessarily synonamous 
and may be attributed to simply geography and the lack of other close day 
noises while out there near the site.I think that part is always a 
constant.I sure wish someone else were here to listen to these things.Maybe 
they are calling me and I will be zapped into the

Good day to all members, I hope all is well . I've been pondering some of my 
tone descriptions and I would like to add something which I hope will help 
or at least clarify what I hear, since a few others are hearing the 2 tones 
as I do.The tones are the same, as I have posted before but to clarify, let 
me say this: The low tone is obviously at the low end of our human hearing 
range or slightly out of that range, and the high tone is somewhere at about 
2 octaves higher than (up scale from)the low tone. This is the range of 
where these are, for me, from this site.For the benefit of those who may be 
more musically inclined or who have studied music or are just a home 
musician, the descriptions I have given were derived from my own musical 
talent.For example, if someone were thinking the tones were located 
somewhere in relationship to a standard keyboard, I have yet to devise a 
method to locate the tones with respect or reference to the keyboard.So it 
is only with my musical experiance that I can only guess at the actual 
distance between the 2 tones, but I think it is a fair assessment to say 
that they are about 2 octaves from each other.The way I hear them and then 
vocalize them out loud,I know that I'm not in the actual "key" or range, but 
there is about that 2 octave distance between them.So in other words, the 
low tone in not that high up on the keyboard, or anywhere near "middle C" 
.So as we are listening quietly for tones and hums, this is how I first 
became aware of them, it was musical and very low and it was the low tone 
which first caught my attention, then about a couple days later, during the 
night, I was blown away to discover the higher tone. Comments anyone?? I 
must re-read some of the postings again, but I appreciate who it was that 
sent the message that middle C was equal to a certain frequency, and they 
listed the frequency. One last thought.. I can verifiably say that 
pertaining to geographical locations for me to hear the tones, I DO actually 
hear them from a S.E. mountainous location, which is about 30 miles away. I 
think that location is still within the same small foothills of that 
mountain range, so its possible the tones are resonating throughout the 
mountains. A few months ago I was not certain if I could hear them from any 
other direction other than North. They seemed to be very faint, even though 
I was in a guiet spot in the woods. So Wes, my hats off to you,in that there 
might be a proximity/ distance factor relating to closeness and/ or strength 
of broadcast.And I agree that perhaps another factor is the 
"country/rural/vs. city/population " application to the tones and hums we 
are hearing.For me to be up here in the woods and still have a hard time 
hearing them sometimes, then how much more difficult for others in / near 
industrialized areas to hear them!! I think I can concure with others who 
live near cities, that the power and technology causing this phenomanon, 
might be powerful enough to transmit along any chosen medium like pipes or 
lines etc.The frequency broadcast just might be resonating along these 
mediums. If your location is too noisy to actually hear tones, then maybe 
your hum is captured by the pipes and lines.In comparison to my location and 
my house,I dont have any resonating effect to report. Within my house,the 
tones  dont vibrate anything and it doesnt matter in the direction I am 
facing. It is an all wood structure and I have tried to put my ears to the 
walls but then I can really hear the outside day noises very clearly, but 
that doesnt change the tones, they are very independant of anything else. 
Thoughts ?? Rick

no problem Rick,

the components are:
L....ferrite wound coil (like the ones in AM radios)
D....germanium diode, 1N34, AA119, OA91
C....1nF
P1...470k
P2...1k
R1, R2...1k5
T....2N3819
B....9V
The meter movement should be reasonably good sensitivity like 500 uA or better.
Use P1 for adjusting the sensitivity and P2 for nulling the meter movement.
Connect the minus terminal of the meter with the drain of the FET transistor.
I forgot to add a little on/off switch - this goes in line with the battery of
course.

Just in case you take your sensitivity meter too close to the transmitter
antenna, you might smoke the diode! To prevent this just add a pair of silicon
diodes antiparallel across the coil.
Have fun.
cheers, Peter.

Rick.. maybe this will help.. the relationship between two musical
notes (or tones) is known as an interval.. a "perfect" octave is a
mod-2 relation, ie: "a-440" is a popular reference for middle "A,"
while "a-220" is one octave down, and "a-880" is one octave up..

Other common intervals include the major 3rd, which is 4 half steps
above a fundamental, the perfect 4th which is 5 half steps up, and
the perfect 5th which is 7 half-steps above a fundamental.  The
major 3rd is prononced in the opening of "Dixi," while the 4th
is well heard in "Here Comes the Bride," and the 5th is the 
turn-around (sequal to refrain) in traditional 12-bar rock..

Why did ET make such a big deal about the "perfect 5th" in the
film Close Encounters?  In the purest of all music, it seems it
would be sinful to utilize non-integral intervals.. in the early
tradition (and in Oriental penta-tonic scales), the intervals of 
notes were/are based on integer relations of frequency; ie: 1/2,
4/3, and 3/4... BUT in modern music we are forced to frequently
change keys and thus have moved into an "almost=perfect" 12 note
equally tempered scale which enables transpostion...

Problem with "perfect" pitch is mechanical.. the equally
tempered scale uses the 12th root of two to maintain perfect
octaves over a wide range, but p5s & p4s which should come out
as rational 1.25s and 1.33..s wind up 1.24... & 1.33334!!! and
having played guitar for 30 years with as much power as a mis-
firing Volkswaggon engine I am quite convinced it will take
ET beings (or drugs to curb awareness?) to straighten it out! 

   S. Klabis in Phoenix AZ / 
 "flying saucer loudspeakers" at <http://www.scn.org/~sak/>
