Robert and Dorothy, some facts that may help:

Code Red only affects servers, not home computers. See
http://cnet.com/software/0-5067630-8-6717594-1.html?tag=ld

Make sure you're running an up-to-date virus checker (Norton AntiVirus,
http://www.symantec.com/nav/nav_9xnt is recommended) and firewall (ZoneAlarm
is recommended, free at http://www.zonelabs.com). Without those, your
computer is wide open to any hacker in the world. Take the Shields Up test
at https://grc.com/x/ne.dll?bh0bkyd2 to test your vulnerability. You may be
shocked to learn how vulnerable you are if you don't have a firewall.

>no problem Rick,
>
>the components are:
>L....ferrite wound coil (like the ones in AM radios)
>D....germanium diode, 1N34, AA119, OA91
>C....1nF
>P1...470k
>P2...1k
>R1, R2...1k5
>T....2N3819
>B....9V
>The meter movement should be reasonably good sensitivity like 500 uA or 
>better.
>Use P1 for adjusting the sensitivity and P2 for nulling the meter movement.
>Connect the minus terminal of the meter with the drain of the FET 
>transistor.
>I forgot to add a little on/off switch - this goes in line with the battery 
>of
>course.
>
>Just in case you take your sensitivity meter too close to the transmitter
>antenna, you might smoke the diode! To prevent this just add a pair of 
>silicon
>diodes antiparallel across the coil.
>Have fun.
>cheers, Peter.

Dorthy:  I do respect your wishes.  I generally consider any news-
group open to the public, but at this point in time I will continue 
to delete all pertinent postings from my email, unless you, the 
author of your own work specifically advise to pass a word.
 
Regarding my global objective, I began an independent study of bio-
logical radiation hazards in 1985, directly proceding the death of 
my father.  My father, a WW2 US-Army veteran, worked as a Millwright 
machinist and electrician for about 40 years, mostly in the states 
of Michigan and California.  Upon retirement in 1978 he moved to an 
unsettled suburb 20 miles east of Phoenix Arizona and discovered 
within a couple months that his new house contained faulty wiring.  
Fighting with officials for truth about the problems, he was 
challenged on grounds of ordinance and finally gave up entirely.
 
Me?  In 1973 I flunked my eye test with the USAF and went to work 
as a civilian with the ISCET and the FCC in the electronic industry. 
A startling awareness in the mid '80s struck against my sanity as I 
began to believe (and talk about) mysterious forces I sincerely 
believed harmful.  Then moving in with my own mother for mutual 
support I began to face the same fire as my father.  
 
By 1989 I realized I would have to fight war at home.  My sister, 
then on active USAF duty at WAFB was leaving due to base closure,
and I began spilling allegations about communist invasion.  Later
that year, galvonic measurements I made of ground loop activity
got even more believable, but certain on-lookers made accusations
of the practice of witchcraft and my experiments abruptly halted 
after being petitioned for mental health evaluation to Tucson.
 
Around October 1989 my case was finally laughed out of court, and 
I was offered training and employment as a counselor-assistant at 
a substance abuse rehabilitation center near Casa Grande.  By 1991 
our US "ADA" proposed a conflict entailing law enforcement verses
the mental health system at which time I began collecting SSI and 
took a federal grant to return to school.  
 
To make a long story short, in 1998 I finished my AGS, and learned
I would have to be very careful working with mother nature.. most
especially amidst divers crowds of people!  Our nation's military 
are an indispensable entity of government designed to uphold human 
rights in time of war.  As necessary an "evil" to dealve into the 
depths of our planet earth, truths which could be mis-interpreted 
by otherwise innocent by-standers might cause panic situations .. 
thus I accept: SECRETS do prevail..
  
Said realization may be dis-heartening to those adept to assembling
pieces of rumors, but if actions speak louder than words, and words 
speak louder than thought, then it seems generally safer our free-
speaking nation should FEEL FREE to vent thought in literal words, 
rather than take liberties at silent-imprudent actions.  Of course
the Bible says I should not bear false witness AGAINST my neighbor. 
But if some enemy FORCES me to tell a lie and I am only free to do 
as I am told then why waste energy worrying about the world?

I just subscribed to the list, just discovered the hum page today, and so am 
fairly uninformed but quite intrigued. But please, don't push me off as a 
nonhearer just yet.

I'm 19 years old, and aside from practically disappeared bronchial asthma, a 
perfectly healthy female.

Around the time of the collapse of the USSR (I was about 10 years old at the 
time) my father and I watched a lot of CSPAN and CNN. We had cable TV (now 
have Direct TV). During at least a 6 month period around the collapse of the 
USSR (it's one of those "life moments" like the JFK assasination, for me), 
any time that we had CNN on at home, I could hear a distinctive humming -- 
I'd say between a 4 and 5. I would ask dad (he would be in the room, usually 
I would be in the hallway) if he heard it -- no. Mom -- no. At the same 
time, when visiting my grandparents house in a slightly more upscale 
neighborhood than our own, when they had CNN on, I heard the same thing, but 
pushing more toward a 5. Again, they did not hear it, and my grandparents 
have almost perfect hearing (even 9 years later I still don't have to repeat 
myself). It drove me nuts, and even going to my room on the opposite end of 
the house did not rid me of the sensation of buzzing that had accompanied 
it.

I had heard and have heard this same type of hum, to a lower scale, for 
brief moments in time before and after this period of time had occured, but 
I have never thought much of it, as I have been subject to a wide variety of 
phenomenon in my life and figured it just one of those things my head did.

In the past year, I have experienced practically 0 hum, partially I think 
because I'm on my computer a lot and it makes quite a bit of noise (so much 
I can't hear the phone sometimes) that replicates humming, whirrings, and 
ringings. I tend to block all this noise out then.

HOWEVER...in this past year I have had, chronically, what I have been 
calling "morning migraines". My typical sleeping hours are between 11pm and 
5:30am (7am on mornings I sleep in). I will sleep in a normal position but 
wake up with INTENSE pressure on my head, to an effect that I have assumed 
that I have simply rammed my head into the pillow while sleeping (it's the 
best assumption I had ;) ) This develops into a highly painful migraine that 
will not go away with any amount of headache medication, sleep, head 
massages, etc. It usually lasts from 5-11 hours -- I have had only two cases 
out of dozens where it has lasted past 5pm. I have changed sleep positions 
several times, and have only two comfortable ones left to try with my body 
pillow; no position has lent itself to be headache free. Other symptoms that 
come with this headache are blurry thought and vision, highly tense/weak 
muscles, stomach sickness/nausea, and loss of direction. I can suffer 
migraines if I get too much light in my eyes, but they are NOTHING like 
this.

I know that this isn't a migraine discussion group, but I have a strong 
feeling now that these absolutely unexplainable migraines (i've now gotten 
two in the middle of the day!!) are related to the hum, or perhaps something 
similar. As I've said, I used to hear the hum sporadically except for that 
regularity with CNN...but I have been shutting out these kinds of noises for 
the same amount of time that I've  been having these migraines.

I live in Southern CA, a suburb of Los Angeles, and not really close at all 
to any military base. Observing military craft in my area (even at the 
college I attend) is very rare. There is an airport somewhere nearby that I 
can see the airplanes coming in for landing at through my window.

So what's the diagnosis? Should I not assume hum, but try to listen for it 
more? After all, I do go to a state college (if the conspiracy theories are 
true)...

Jaime Brownyard
Whittier CA

Hi Rick,

what I would do in your case is to make the signals of this transmitter visible
and compare them to the audible tones in real time.
Equipment you'd need is a scope meter, an audio mixer and an oscillator.
Alternatively you could use a laptop PC running an FFT program on it instead of
the scope meter.
This has several advantages - and doesn't have to come dearer.
Either scope or laptop (with integrated sound processor of course) you can buy
for a couple hundred bucks second hand.
The audio mixer and oscillator would have to be a home brew project costing not
more than 5...10 bucks.

This setup would enable you to see the modulation (most likely MSK) on the scope
or more elegantly on the FFT display on the laptop.
cheers, Peter.

  Hello my name is John and I live in the Portland, Oregon area.  I =
first heard the hum in 1979, and until a couple of days ago I had no =
idea how wide spread this problem is.  Except for my wife and son, who =
have heard the hum on occasion, I knew of no one else.  I was =
embarrassed by the fact that I heard the hum when no one else did.  I =
find it interesting that some residents of Toas, NM started to hear the =
hum in I think it was 1991, which then started an investigation.  But =
yet I was hearing it in 1979.  I wonder if there are any documented =
complaints going that far back.  When I started hearing this sound it =
was at night.  At that time it would start at about 11pm and continue on =
until early morning.  I went through the procedures of shutting off all =
power to the house and even had the local power company come out and =
shut off a power transformer located in front of our house.  None of =
this helped.  We then moved to the country and after a few days I =
started hearing the hum again.  Again I called the power company to shut =
down a transformer that sits on a mound a few feet in front of my house =
and feeds solely my house.  This was no help.  Now I hear this hum =
constantly day and night.  It will sometimes go away for a few days but =
then it returns.  I have tried to coordinate this with weather =
conditions, i.e. rain, sunshine, humidity.. it doesn't seem to matter.  =
I have also heard this hum in Lakewood, CO and in Phoenix, AZ.  Last =
spring my wife and I spent 4 days in Albuquerque, NM and I didn't hear =
it at all.  Can you tell me (1) what if any investigations are going on =
at the present time to locate the source of the hum (2) has anyone come =
out with a way to block out the hum (I have had custom earplugs made and =
I tried playing the radio low..the plugs hurt my ears after a couple of =
hours of sleeping with them in and the radio keeps me awake) (3) does =
someone have a list of other discussion groups that I can join or web =
sites that I can visit that deal with this problem.  I'm not a =
scientist, I know nothing about radio transmissions or anything like =
that, so I can't offer any help other than support.  Lately this hum has =
been really loud to me.  In the last few days it's there but it seems to =
be distant.  Thanks for taking the time to read this.      =20
=20



    =20

Hello John, welcome to this web.Continue to read these posts and you will 
come up to speed with these discussions. In the meanwhile, you are probably 
hearing what most of us are hearing, as far as the general catagory of noise 
or hum.   Depending on the global locations,the noise/hum/tones are slightly 
different but I feel they are representative of the same type of technology 
and broadcast frequencies being used. Whether by private communication 
companies, we arent sure of, but being used by the military, THAT we are 
sure of.You describe similar characteristics to the tones I hear up here, 
North of Seattle, Wa.Do you consider it to be more like a single hum or 
possibly a 2 tone sound? Its very interesting that you describe it as being 
distant. For all others here,this "distance" factor concures with the way I 
perceive these Tones ,as well.I hear 2 distinct tones which appear to be 
distant and tend to not focus on them when I'm trying to sleep.I dont have a 
problem with the noise as long as I dont focus intently on them. I had to 
keep my bedroom door open for a couple of weeks, or a few days, to let the 
refrigerator noise drown out the tones during the nights.This is what it 
took for me to break my concentration / awareness cycle so I could sleep. I 
have identified these Tones I hear, as coming from a military communications 
site up here, but havent proved whether the tones are a direct result of the 
broadcasts,in real time, or if the tones are within my head but caused by 
the certain frequencies being broadcasted by these Towers.Either way,this 
location is what is causing the Tones up here.Scout around down there and 
canvass your area looking for some sort of tower site, or a group of smaller 
towers, something unusual. If your hum is coming from up here, then maybe 
you are just in the path of the broadcasts being sent toward the South East 
direction, probably the S.W. Pacific Ocean or Hawaii.Are you feeling any 
other physical symptoms? I am not. Rick

>that I heard the hum when no one else did.  I find it interesting that some 
>residents of Toas, NM started to hear the hum in I think it was 1991, which 
>then started an investigation.  But yet I was hearing it in 1979.  I wonder 
>if there are any documented complaints going that far back.  When I started 
>hearing this sound it was at night.  At that time it would start at about 
>11pm and continue on until early morning.  I went through the procedures of 
>shutting off all power to the house and even had the local power company 
>come out and shut off a power transformer located in front of our house.  
>None of this helped.  We then moved to the country and after a few days I 
>started hearing the hum again.  Again I called the power company to shut 
>down a transformer that sits on a mound a few feet in front of my house and 
>feeds solely my house.  This was no help.  Now I hear this hum constantly 
>day and night.  It will sometimes go away for a few days but then it 
>returns.  I have tried to coordinate this with weather conditions, i.e. 
>rain, sunshine, humidity.. it doesn't seem to matter.  I have also heard 
>this hum in Lakewood, CO and in Phoenix, AZ.  Last spring my wife and I 
>spent 4 days in Albuquerque, NM and I didn't hear it at all.  Can you tell 
>me (1) what if any investigations are going on at the present time to 
>locate the source of the hum (2) has anyone come out with a way to block 
>out the hum (I have had custom earplugs made and I tried playing the radio 
>low..the plugs hurt my ears after a couple of hours of sleeping with them 
>in and the radio keeps me awake) (3) does someone have a list of other 
>discussion groups that I can join or web sites that I can visit that deal 
>with this problem.  I'm not a scientist, I know nothing about radio 
>transmissions or anything like that, so I can't offer any help other than 
>support.  Lately this hum has been really loud to me.  In the last few days 
>it's there but it seems to be distant.  Thanks for taking the time to read 
>this.

John,

Two things have worked well for me.  Having an exhaust fan run in another
room.   Set is up to pull air from the outside, through the room you sleep
in.  It seems to me that if the air is moving, it is somehow reduced.  This
works well as long as the outside temperature allows it.  The second thing
that works well, is a white/pink noise generator.  A small one will cost you
$100.00 and you can get them from places like Sharper Image.  They can be
set up to make different sounds, ie: wind, rain, waterfall, etc.

You are not alone !!

Richard

Jaime,

I know exactly what you are saying about the morning migraines.  Too much
partying the night before...just kidding.

A couple of things that you can try, that sometimes helps me.  Sleep with
socks on.  For some reason this seems to help reduce my headaches.  And
another symptom that I have but you did not mention, is that my eyes feel
like they are too hot.  I wear glasses, I it seems like my eyes are on fire.
I take off my glasses and run them under cold water, and that also seems to
help.  My vision also seems blurry during the peak of pain. 

Hope this helps, 
Richard

> cases

> 
> several times, and have only two comfortable ones left to try with my body
> 
> pillow; no position has lent itself to be headache free. Other symptoms

and forth, is exactly what I describe up here too.I think I would recommend 
a very passive approach to dealing with these noises/tones, by using white 
noise generators or breaking your awareness cycle, or whatever it takes to 
not be affected by those hums/tones. The reason being, if you start to make

results.Especially when you (we) cant prove anything or have any evidence.

Hi John, how are you? I was wondering, if you plotted the location of your 
house currently, as well as your previous house, are the two locations 
directly in-line, geographically speaking? I still wonder if you are simply 
"in the line of fire" from wherever the noise is coming from. There may not 
be a connection to the location of the radio tower, if it is really a radio 
tower. One can usually tell how they look so I take your word that it is a 
radio tower. Unless its a NORAN boating signal tower,we arent sure if we can 
eleminate those types of towers as being a source, currently I think it is 
still an open option to explore. Other than the hum you are experiancing, 
your location sounds like a dream, I'm slightly envious, you know??!!! From 
up there, you might be more suseptable to picking up other broadcasts but 
I'll bet your normal radio signals are very clear too! Also, from up there, 
you might want to study the sky-line late at night to see if you can see any 
red beacon lights in all directions. Use binocullars. Look for a small 
cluster of lights , these would indicate other Towers which you might not 
have noticed before. I used this same technique to locate the Towers I 
observe up here. I found 8 on one ridge and 6 on the other ridge, these are 
connected by wires up at the tops of them, and this is the large "dish" 
formed, which is about 3/4 of a mile across!!!! Some dish, hmmm?? I'm only 
speculating the possibility that you are hearing hums/tones from the same 
source as I am, your descriptions sound simular to mine and I believe this 
site here, has the power to produce that kind of result from a great 
distance.Study the noise you hear and try to define its certain 
characteristics, plot the locations you verifiably say are consistant, where 
you hear the tones/hum. You are also correct in your observations, that 
sometimes the tones are less strong than other times, and as I have found, 
at times they are completly silent too.This is a very rare occasion. Even 
though they are always broadcasting, it doesnt bother me too much but I have 
to be careful to not concentrate on them so intently, or I would be 
conscious of them all the time.They are still there, whenever I stop and 
listen, providing the day noises dont drown out the noise.Keep in touch. 
Rick

tones whether I am at home or in the mountains... thats another thing, I 
think the frequency travels with the ground or eminates from the ground and 
the specific terrain/ mountainous regions act like a resonator, to aid in 
the travel of those signals. I think we are dealing with a man-made 
phenomonan and since I think its military, in my case, I can definitatly say

Hi Robert, how are you? You are right, this site is still active, but of 
course I already knew that and its good to let others know of that too. I 
would like to say that according to my observations here, the site is not 
like any other you can imagine. Its based into the foothills with a small 
unobtrusive link gate, with a small guard shack. This site serves as a day 
recreation resort for military personnell( active and retired). Tall fir 
trees surround all of the entire foothills ,with the area under the Towers 
and wires kept clear of any or much, vegitation.It is on a small back-road 
dead-end paved road which leads directly to this main gate. There is no 
other way in or out.I dont believe there are many personnell stationed 
there, but usually when I drive up that road, I notice some older, salty 
marine type fellows driving to or from the site.I have never observed any 
air traffic and there is not a landing strip in there. This is used for 
communications only( or other broadcast purposes).I'm sure these are the 
guys in charge of either running the place or the marines who guard the 
entire grounds and surrounding forrests. I dont see much activity, per say, 
only the occasional personal vehicle coming to or from the base. This is not 
like your standard concept of what a military base would look like,busy with 
normal activity, trucks, deliveries, open to the public, etc.There are not 
any buildings that can be seen from the main gate either. If you check the 
"Terraserver.com" you can see some grounds buildings inside. There are 
usually about 50 marines on board a US Naval vessel so for this site, I 
would imagine maybe that same number, to roam the surrounding hills and 
grounds, to keep others out!! This land is completly surrounded by fir trees 
and burried into the hills, boardered on all sides, by fir trees and low 
foothills, leading toward the bigger mountains, further in the distance. 
Some of the logs have been cleared by the loggers and you can see patches of 
the cleared spots. These logging plots boarder the site on all sides,some 
close, some not, but I'll bet if one tried to gain access to the clear-cut 
locations via the public logging roads, one would be visited by the M.I.B. 
at a certain point in distance from the perimeter.Scarry indeed!!! Later. 
Rick

Adam, 
Personally, from my research into ancient history I honestly do not believe Satan exists.  I believe he is an invention of the Judeo Christian schools of thought.  My feeling is that he is an excuse for the evil in men's hearts, of which, God knows, there

 is enough to need an excuse. 
But don't let me paint this too darkly either, I believe that there is good in men's hearts as well.  After all, Yin/Yang - you must have the negative for the positive to exist.  The negative must also exist in order for a choice to be possible or necessa

ry. 
But I do, as you mentioned, believe that they are here, and have been for a long time.  I also believe that one of the strongest arguments in their favor is the Great Pyramid.  Even with todays technology we would not be able to duplicate the feat today. 

 And these folks were supposed to have done it without steel? 
Also, one of the standard methods of dating (Radio-carbon dating does not work on Monuments, only on the degradable materials found at the same level with the artifacts.  Even so, interpretation of the results of Radio-Carbon dating is under wide variance

 and in heated dispute.) for archeologists when looking at huge structures with celestial orientation - especially those with massive sized stones - is to back-date to see when the celestial alignment is precisely correct, thus giving a date for the build

ing of the structure.  When you do this same back-dating on the Great Pyramid it dates to 10,000 BC.  Way before we were supposed to have formed the first real civilization.  With the Egyptian accuracy that has been touted for centurys, I feel that this b

ack-dating method can be trusted here if nowhere else.  This would make the G.P. the first Pyramid built and not the last, and built before our time as well. 
Then we have the unique design of the G.P.  We all know that none of these structures were used as tombs, so what was the G.P.s purpose?  And what about the Great Hall with it's recesses that used to house different sorts of crystals.  What did they do?  

If nothing, why were they removed before the G.P. was sealed up?  Tomb Robbers someone mentioned ?   Except that we have historical records of finding the various, camouflaged, passages and know that no one had been in there beforehand.  If they had, they

 would have hadto have restored the Pyramid exactly the way it was built, leaving no traces. 
Did we build the pyramid with primitive tools?  I just can't swallow it.  Could we build it today?  Nope! 
Too many questions and too many mysteries for Academia to be quite so confident! 
Whether these Aliens are good or bad?  I think you are looking at things as if they are black and white.  I find that things are usually more in terms of shades of grey.  However, if you wish to discuss this idea more, contact me off list.  It is safer.

            Wednesday, August 22 11:00 AM SGT
            Mysterious maddening buzzing probed in southwest Germany
            KARLSRUHE, Germany, Aug 22 (AFP) -
           
Hundreds of people in Germany's southwest are being driven to distraction
by a mysterious nocturnal buzzing noise -- seriously enough for the local
authorities to decide to investigate the matter scientifically. 

Many have been complaining of racing pulse and fatigue along with a sense
of excitation and uncontrollable muscle quivering during their resulting
insomnia. 

"Often at night I feel as if my bed were electrically charged. The pillow,
the mattress and my whole body vibrate, and the only thing you want to do
is to be able to turn off that sound," said one of the sufferers, Carmen
Mischke. 

>From Lake Constance to Heidelberg, the environment department of the
Baden-Wuerttemberg state government has been hearing similar stories from

Now the authorities have commissioned the physicist Henriche Menges to
take a closer look at ten out of 300 homes which have reported the
phenomenon. 

If one were to believe the authors of the German website
www.raum-und-zeit.de, the source of the mysterious buzzing sound in the
ears of afflicted citizens is a US military project named HAARP based in
Alaska. 

There the US military are supposed to have built a kind of giant energy
accelerator whose electro-magnetic waves could be used as a super-weapon
to "make a nation dance on one leg" or drive a whole city of people
insane. 

Menges has no time right now for such fantastic-sounding theories.  "We
are starting off with the likelier explanations and leaving the more
speculative ones aside," he answered politely when asked what he thought
about that particular idea. 

The scientist is tracking down the buzzing equipped with a
microphone and sensors able to detect low-frequency vibrations.

He said that such deep buzzing sounds could come from diesel motors,
aircraft, waterfalls or compressors as used in refrigerators and
air-conditioning equipment. But wind blowing over chimneys could also act
as a giant organ pipe, he said. 

The human ear can detect sounds as low as 20-40 hertz, and the microphone
Menges and his team are using can detect sounds as low as eight hertz,
while the vibration sensors are sensitive to as low as three hertz. 

This is important because human internal organs are sensitive to
vibrations as low as between six to 12 hertz and can detect them. 

Menges believes that the buzzing or booming is due to sound waves because
of the sensitivity of people's ears and abdomens to them. He has ruled out
electromagnetic waves such as those emitted by portable telephones because
they are nothing like enough intense enough. 

Low-frequency sound waves on the other hand can be propagated over a
distance of kilometres (miles) and can even pass through thick concrete,
making identification of the source difficult. 

Work in Germany on measuring the phenomenon is expected to continue into
the autumn. 

Whether the mystery will be elucidated is uncertain, even for Menges. A
similar one in the small town of Taos in the US state of New Mexico was
investigated in the early 1990s without result, he pointed out. 

A "Working Group for Investigation of the Buzzing Sound", which says
people in the Saarland and North Rhine-Westphalia regions of western says
people in the Saarland and North Rhine-Westphalia regions of western
Germany have had similar experiences, reckons that the cause is likely due
to low-frequency sound vibrations. 

However it says that a "very long-frequency electro-magnetic field"  of
between 0.5 to 50 hertz has also been measured in the region and could
point to an explanation. 

The working group has a website with the address www.ohr-geraeusch.de .

http://scrippsnews.ucsd.edu/releases2001/hedlin_infrasound.html

FOR RELEASE: August 22, 2001

NEW SCRIPPS MONITORING DEVICES SET TO DETECT CLANDESTINE NUCLEAR WEAPONS
TESTING
‘Infrasound’ array of instruments picks up meteor’s kiloton blast over the
Pacific

VIDEO

Hedlin on the new infrasound array
Video requires QUICKTIME
A unique array of listening devices deployed by researchers at Scripps
Institution of Oceanography at the University of California, San Diego, is
one of the first stations in an important new global network that will
detect signals from events as diverse as secret nuclear weapons tests,
volcanic eruptions, and hurricanes in early formation.

One of the first significant signals received by the Scripps instruments
resulted from the April 23 explosion of a large meteor crashing into Earth’s
atmosphere. The meteor, reportedly 8- to 12-feet across, exploded with a
yield of a few thousand tons of TNT, nearly the force of the atomic bomb
dropped on Hiroshima.

The Scripps array consists of eight microbarometers spread across two
kilometers at the Cecil and Ida Green Piñon Flat Observatory, located in the
mountains south of Palm Springs, Calif. Each device is equipped with a noise
reduction system that filters unwanted energy from atmospheric turbulence
and increases sensitivity to signals at the "infrasonic" scale that fall
below the 20 hertz level of human hearing. The array records signals that
are too faint, and vary too slowly, to be detected by humans.

The array is one of the first in a planned network of 60 that will play a
vital role in efforts to monitor the globe for clandestine nuclear testing
blasts. The infrasonic network tracks the atmosphere as part of a network
that combines infrasonic signal tracking with seismic stations that pick up
signals from the solid earth, hydroacoustic stations that monitor energy in
the oceans, and a radionuclide network that checks the air for radioactive
particles.

"Infrasound energy tracking was big business in the 50s and 60s, when there
was a lot of nuclear testing in the atmosphere," said Michael Hedlin,
associate researcher at the Cecil H. and Ida M. Green Institute of
Geophysics and Planetary Physics at Scripps, and, with Jon Berger, a lead
scientist in the Piñon Flat infrasound array development. "Interest in
infrasound decreased when nuclear testing moved underground. Now infrasound
monitoring has re-emerged in importance due to the number of countries that
may be capable of developing nuclear weapons. We need to monitor around the
globe."

Hedlin says an infrasonic network is capable of providing data not only from
nuclear blasts, but from a variety of natural phenomena that may become
useful in scientific research.

This was the case on April 23, when the large meteor crashed into the
atmosphere over the Pacific Ocean several hundred miles west of Baja
California.

"If this rock had come into the atmosphere at a slightly different time, it
might have exploded not over the Pacific, but over a large metropolitan
area," said Hedlin. "With this global listening network we can develop much
better statistics on large meteors and get a better idea of how often these
massive objects enter the atmosphere."

Large explosions send part of their acoustic energy into the audible range,
but those signals dissipate rapidly. They also emit large amounts of energy
into the infrasonic range in signals that decay slowly across vast
distances. Thus the April 23 explosion was prominently featured 1,800
kilometers away on the Piñon Flat instruments. The signals were also
recorded approximately 11,000 kilometers away by an infrasound array in
Germany.

In addition to meteors, infrasonic energy is generated by chemical
explosions, supersonic aircraft, tornadoes, landslides, earthquakes, and
volcanoes.

"Our colleagues in Japan have learned that minor volcanic eruptions of magma
or gas might be missed seismically but produce strong acoustic signals,"
said Hedlin. "Seismic and infrasound data taken together give a much fuller
account of activity inside the volcano that might be indicative of an
impending, significant eruption."

VIDEO

Hedlin on the meteor explosion
Video requires QUICKTIME
A new infrasonic array is set to be deployed in Cape Verde, a location off
the coast of Africa known as a nursery for brewing hurricanes. As the
hurricanes develop and emit infrasonic signals, Hedlin believes such data
might contribute to early detection.

"There is a lot going on in the atmosphere that we need to know more about.
The infrasound network will offer us an unprecedented opportunity to better
understand these phenomena on a global scale. We anticipate that this global
network of listening posts that monitors Earth’s fluid exterior shell where
we live will some day become as indispensable as the global seismic network
that monitors the Earth’s solid interior for seismic activity."

Although the Scripps group provided the closest observations of the meteor,
the event was analyzed by a consortium of universities and laboratories. The
explosion was first noticed by a group at Los Alamos National Laboratory.
Early characterization of the event was done by the Los Alamos group, the
Center for Monitoring Research, the University of Hawaii, and the University
of Alaska.

The consortium is led by Henry Bass at the University of Mississippi.
Construction of the array was supported by the Defense Threat Reduction
Agency (DTRA), the Provisional Technical Secretariat (PTS) of the UN
Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty Office in Vienna, and the US Army Space and
Missile Defense Command (SMDC) University Research Initiative (URI).
Distribution statement ‘A,’ approved for public release — distribution
unlimited.

          Adam,=20

          Personally, from my research into ancient history I honestly =
do not believe Satan exists.  I believe he is an invention of the Judeo =
Christian schools of thought.  My feeling is that he is an excuse for =
the evil in men's hearts, of which, God knows, there is enough to need =
an excuse.=20

          But don't let me paint this too darkly either, I believe that =
there is good in men's hearts as well.  After all, Yin/Yang - you must =
have the negative for the positive to exist.  The negative must also =
exist in order for a choice to be possible or necessary.=20

          But I do, as you mentioned, believe that they are here, and =
have been for a long time.  I also believe that one of the strongest =
arguments in their favor is the Great Pyramid.  Even with todays =
technology we would not be able to duplicate the feat today.  And these =
folks were supposed to have done it without steel?=20

          Also, one of the standard methods of dating (Radio-carbon =
dating does not work on Monuments, only on the degradable materials =
found at the same level with the artifacts.  Even so, interpretation of =
the results of Radio-Carbon dating is under wide variance and in heated =
dispute.) for archeologists when looking at huge structures with =
celestial orientation - especially those with massive sized stones - is =
to back-date to see when the celestial alignment is precisely correct, =
thus giving a date for the building of the structure.  When you do this =
same back-dating on the Great Pyramid it dates to 10,000 BC.  Way before =
we were supposed to have formed the first real civilization.  With the =
Egyptian accuracy that has been touted for centurys, I feel that this =
back-dating method can be trusted here if nowhere else.  This would make =
the G.P. the first Pyramid built and not the last, and built before our =
time as well.=20

          Then we have the unique design of the G.P.  We all know that =
none of these structures were used as tombs, so what was the G.P.s =
purpose?  And what about the Great Hall with it's recesses that used to =
house different sorts of crystals.  What did they do?  If nothing, why =
were they removed before the G.P. was sealed up?  Tomb Robbers someone =
mentioned ?   Except that we have historical records of finding the =
various, camouflaged, passages and know that no one had been in there =
beforehand.  If they had, they would have hadto have restored the =
Pyramid exactly the way it was built, leaving no traces.=20

          Did we build the pyramid with primitive tools?  I just can't =
swallow it.  Could we build it today?  Nope!=20

          Too many questions and too many mysteries for Academia to be =
quite so confident!=20

          Whether these Aliens are good or bad?  I think you are looking =
at things as if they are black and white.  I find that things are =
usually more in terms of shades of grey.  However, if you wish to =
discuss this idea more, contact me off list.  It is safer.=20

Hello to all, hope things are well. I wanted to share something I came 
across about 3 months ago and made some startling comparisons regarding the 
hum/tones and the frequencies used. Please check this web site out: 
www.electric-words.com/cell/research/laisingh/memory1.html  This web site 
shows a study released which covers the topic of exposure to certain 
frequencies and how it relates to tissue and cell damage. The entire article 
is very dry reading but I feel that if we read between the lines we can make 
a connection between the existance of the technology vs. the physical 
affects of exposure. Granted, the study deals with mobile cell phone/ mast 
exposure, RFR exposure to laboratory rats and the collection of data 
relating to the physical symptoms induced by the exposure.The study shows 
that certain biological symptoms occure, both temporary and permanent. These 
frequencies can damage cell growth, can cause DNA strands to deplete, and 
can cause calcium loss, memory loss, and a host of other things, including 
SPECIFICALLY the heating of the inner ear causing a false "hearing" effect!! 
Isnt that related to this discussion, RFR making some of us think we hear 
the hums and tones!!!??? My point in this post is to make aware, the minute 
but tangible coorelation between these frequencies and tissue damage. Think 
about it, if it affects animal tissue then it should affect human tissue as 
well.I feel the small mention to calcium loss can be expanded in the 
following manner: on other web sites, leading into the possible psychotronic 
applications used by the M.I.B., and reported by many people who report to 
be victims,the discussion of being subjected to certain frequencies, these 
victims testify they heard bones snapping, both in their heads (inner ear 
equalizations ?)and in their bodys as well, after being subjected to these 
frequencies! I believe the article I listed only begins to open the 
pandora's box into this technology, how it is being used, and if/how its 
being used against we citizens.Look at the Tennessee episode,as well as 
other strange things happening to local, normal people everywhere.These 
effects are cumulitive, as shown in the studies. So if some of us are having 
physical symptoms every day by being exposed to these RFR's, that may be a 
small "something" to offer to the scientific community, to get some 
attention to this phenomanon which is being produced by our technology but 
is being used against us.I'm lucky, in that I dont have any other symptoms 
to describe. However, I am very tired, lately, of the constant Tones which I 
hear. Maybe I've started to concentrate on them again, I dont know, but at 
times they have been very loud. I know they boost the power to make their 
communications, and I think that the force or field which I felt was coming 
from/ through the ground from the Towers, unless it was specifically a 
microwave beam which I stepped into.This site is awesome in the power that 
it must take to make this happen. This weekend I re-visited the locations 
which I have plotted and didnt feel anything, and the audible level of the 
tones was somewhat disappointing, not as loud as I have experianced 
previously.I'm trying to duplicate the force field effect but have not been 
timely.Anyway, let me know what you think about the article... I dont think 
its a far stretch from where we all are with this topic.I hope you all have 
a good day. Rick

Hello Everyone,

I too, thought the list had disappeared.  I hope everyone's doing as well as 
can be expected.  Rick,  I reviewed the article you suggested and am not 
surprised.  Practically all we're experiencing and others can be traced to 
Electromagnetic Fields and Frequencies, even many of the muscularskeltal and 
fibromyalgia health related problems, just to name a few.  Peter's experiment 
involving the ear shed some resourceful information.  I'm on a couple of 
lists that have not only confirmed this info, but documented it.  Whether 
we're dealing with high or low frequencies, "frequencies" are the operative 
word.

Last week made a significant discovery;  a member on another list suggested 
using a radio on AM Channels.  The sounds that came through was phenomenal.  
First nothing but aloud droning and humming; then a long, piercing signal; 
audible soundwaves reverberating with up and down tones; low and behold; 
sounds of an aircraft-possibly a helicopter(all very audible through the AM 
stations on the radio-no music from any station until the aircraft appeared). 
 Finally some stations cleared, but between them the same unusual sounds.  
Finally, my smoke detector started picking up some of the same sounds, short 
beeps and your could hear sounds as if data from a fax machine was going 
through the smoke detector.  Called the FCC and even allowed them to listen.  
Presently, they're short of funds and have no plans to return to Tennessee to 
investigate.  They were here, Dyersburg, and Union City earlier this year.

Dorothy

>> >> When harm from cell phones are mentioned, what is considered damaging:  
>>> the frequencies, radiation, signals, what? 

	The frequency of the magnatron oscillator in a microwave
        oven is roughly 3GHz, or 3,000,000,000 cycles per second.
        The frequencies of cell phones run from about 900MHz
        (900,000,000 cycles per second) up to about 2Ghz.  
        
        Since cell phone frequencies are in or near the microwave
        range there is a natural fear that the radiation they
        produce could heat human tissue.  This heat would be
        significant if the cell phone were operating at a high
        power level, but the power associated with communications
        is generally much lower than that used in cooking food.  
	
        Hopefully in the near future we will be switching to a 
        spread-spectrum pulse train communications link which
        distributes energy in the domain of time/frequency,
        thus reducing substantially the risk of cooking ears!
        
>>> 
>>> What's causing signals to come through our regular telephones? 
>>> 
	Ordinarilly, the "twisted pair" telephone line should
        cancel noise generated by proximal radiating fields. 
        Either the noise source is incredibly strong or close
        to phone lines, or the phone lines themselves may be
        faulty.

>>> Lastly, Can AC and DC currents exist in the same field? 
>>> 
        "Direct" current may alternate in intensity and simply
        be called fluctuating DC, while "alternating" current
        may be "biased" with a certain DC component.

        But now when we talk about "fields," we can no longer
        measure current in itself.  One ampers of electrical
        current represents 6.3 e18 electrons passing a single
        point in a conductive path in a second.  

        In dealing with radiation fields, conversely, we are
        only concerned with magnetic lines and static forces,
        while current does not necessarily flow.
             
                  S. Klabis / Phoenix AZ, USA.

Christopher Barnaby wrote:

> Has anyone heard it in major cities... I cant seem to capture it at all
> here in the city although when I am in the country it is loud and clear
> continuously...

Once you know what to listen for and how to separate it from the
significant city background noise, it can be heard. I have never visited
an eastern city since I started hearing the hum, but of western cities I
have visited it is especially prominent in Denver and Tulsa. The only
city small or large where I failed to hear the hum on at least two tries
in two separate years was Salt Lake City.  I can't say the hum isn't
there. I just was never able to filter out background and traffic noise
to the point I might be able to pick it up. If the hum was present, it
was completely masked.

Judy

realized something ive never thought of .....A TOWER  ..while my uncle and i
were driving on the land i noticed a tower a tall tower  and i sked my uncle
what it was for he said he didnt know, i asked when it was put there and he
said he doesnt know.... the area i walked in is not far from the tower by
car driving 40mph it would take you 3 minutes not far at all never gave the
tower much thought.. remember the govt does not respect native land where
ever it is   some lands are being used for radio active dump sites   seems
our reservation is being used in another way    now R ick  in this same
vacinity i was driving my car and taking pictures out the car window    thet
came out so nice and clear  except one ,,,,, when we were in the area of
this thing the picture had a very strange red glow to itit was not a clear
picture like the otheres dont know if there is a connection or not just dont
know   seems odd the area where we were driving is called devils corner
now rRick i could share a story on big foot that WE SAW  in the same area
scared the crap out of me it did ,,it sure did same for my wife who was with
me at that time maybe laterbut what a strange two legged creature it is and
its still on the reservationfinally let me say this my wife and i were
driving home from bingo  (i play the slots dont like bingo)and while we were
on a long stretch of road we saw a fleat of objects go down in the woods
they had many colored lights my grandmother did not say a word  my wife and
i could not keep our mouths shut we were discussing what we saw my
grandmother sat there so still so quietly    so many things go on there
BOB

Hi JConn2299,

In my area I have met 5 people so far who also can hear/feel a low frequency
noise at various times.
Over the past 3 years I did a number of acoustical experiments and came to the
conclusion that my hum (which might be different to theirs) is not of an acoustic
nature i.e. is not carried to the ear by sound waves.

The hum started for me about 10 years ago. Before this time I lived in different
places 16.000 km away. Today, when I think back, I had never heard hum there. 1.5
years ago I visited some of these places - still not the slightest hint of a hum
there.
In the last 10 years at my present location there were periods which were
completely hum free. These periods lasted for a few days to several months.
My hum can vary in intensity. My wife's hum also varies but not necessarily in
sync with mine.

I can make my hum louder by certain activities like rushing up and down the
stairs several times or by exposing myself to low frequency noise (which also
raises my blood pressure) for a short time after which I hear hum for a few
minutes at an elevated volume and as a rather constant tone.
I can also make the hum briefly disappear by certain head movements.

All the above activities have one thing in common:
they change certain vital sign parameters like the blood pH value temporarily.

I also know that the wavelength of induced electromagnetic energy inside any
living organism is subject to change with blood pH value, salinity of the body
tissue, temperature etc.

Certain cell structures inside our bodies absorb externally induced electrical
energy. The extent of the absorption depends on the wavelength of the applied EM
energy among other factors.
If the cell structure happens to be in connection with the auditory and/or
vestibular system then this induced energy most likely interferes with normal
signals within the sensoneural paths.
If the induced electrical energy carries frequency components which are inside
the tonal range of our hearing then there will most likely be an artificial
impression of a sound.
It is quite likely though that a number of closely spaced RF frequencies
intermodulate inside the sensitive cell structures and produce an audible
frequency.
This explains to me why the tone I hear has something of a resonating quality.
The tones sound like a varying warbling modulation.
If you had a number of years of experimenting with electronics under your belt
you would know what I am talking about.

Now the sensitivity to these hum causing external signals is not the same in
every organism in that the sensitivity is influenced by so many individual
factors. The hum causing factors for one person can be either totally different,
or very similar to another person's set of factors. These factors depend on the
internal makeup of each specimen. The efficacy of these external triggers are
just as individually different as the audible impressions caused by these.
It's a little bit like each of us carrying a fixed tuned radio around. The
channel each one's radio is tuned at, is totally random but fixed for most of the
time. Only if a nearby transmitter by coincidence broadcasts on the same channel
as your radio then you can hear the music.......

.....Even if you prefer calling the hum a condition or a disease, you only catch
a cold if there are bugs.

Last but not least some personal thoughts about JConn2299's consistently counter
active comments like the one in his last posting which
reads...............................
Seems you're jumping to a conclusion before there's conclusive proof, or even
good evidence.  Some report hearing the hum all the time.  Others say it
comes and goes. Those observations seem to be in conflict, wouldn't you say?
....................................................

The wording of such comments reminds me of poorly trained police officers
interrogating a suspect. So immensely undermining, and implying indignity en
masse.

cheers, Peter.

Someone seems awfully sensitive here.  When investigating any phenomenon you 
have to use reason and question assertions. How else do you separate the true 
from the false?

It's always the true believers who resent the analytical questions.  People 
used to dealing with the scientific method have no problem with them and try 
to use such questions to see which hypotheses should be pursued, and which 
should be discarded. 

You know, I find this endlessly amusing. From time to time I have posted 
perfectly fair and reasonable questions like the one above. Often times I've 
seen defensive, emotional reactions like the one from Peter.
Yet recently, someone sent in a post in which they claimed to have seen 
Bigfoot, and there wasn't a peep. In fact, someone wrote in approvingly in 
response.  Do you think a little skepticism was in order there? There's that 
well known saying of Carl Sagan's, "extraordinary claims require 
extraordinary proof."

Instead of resenting questions, one should try to answer them to try to solve 
the puzzle. 

Now watch. Because of my Bigfoot reference we'll see all sorts of posts 
saying, "I have an open mind about such things." But do you really? Or will 
you be applying a healthy dose of skepticism. If you come out tomorrow 
morning and find that all the flowers in your front yard have been smashed to 
the ground and there are big foot prints in your flower bed, and I'm standing 
there saying, "I saw what happened... Bigfoot was here and trampled your 
flower bed...I saw the whole thing"  are you going to believe me?  After all, 
you have not only my testimony, but physical evidence...all those smashed 
flowers. (For that recent poster, we have only his testimony.)  Or, are you 
going to start with a more prosaic explanation. 

If you buy the Bigfoot story without skepticism, then you're at the head of 
the true believer class.  If you start by looking for a more ordinary 
explanation, then you're using my method of analysis.  Something tells me, 
most readers here, in their day to day lives, don't make unsupported leaps of 
faith. 

If I tell you, "I know what happened to Chandra Levy, I saw the whole thing, 
a UFO came down the street, and in broad daylight beamed her aboard and then 
whisked itself away above the clouds," do you find that a perfectly plausible 
explanation? If there's another witness who says he saw two men
hustle Chandra into a white van and then drive off, do you find each account 
of equal credibility?  Or do you rank one above the other in terms of 
plausibility? If they're not equal, what do you use to separate them?

If you're still questioning listeners' hearing, this logic may clear things 
up.  The hum both comes and goes, and it's there all the time it's not gone, 
which is most of the time.  It is a riddle because no one will claim 
responsibility for it.  We need a scientific test.  Say we identify some 
suspect producers of the sound and arrange for them to shut down for a period 
of time and poll the listeners as to whether the sound stops.     
There is a consensus on the nature of the sound.  It has the characteristics 
of high-powered electronics and site-specific broadcasting, like what you'd 
expect to emanate from generators capable of producing the power needed to 
scan the sea and sky.    
The real question is:  do you not recognize that you may be exposed to 
something that may harm you but that you don't perceive?  Air pollution was 
like that once, global warming still is.  Remember lead?  The people who 
suffer that one are sick, yeah.

this question in TB's posting sums it up pretty well:
if something other than sound is capable of tickling your hearing nerves, what
other parts of your body may be affected - of which you have no direct sensation
but may only manifest itself in the longer term in a potentially unpleasant way.
Just consider the facts: studies around the world have shown statistically
significant occurrences of certain diseases around high power TV broadcasting
towers. The same goes for people living along high voltage power lines and near
high power transformers. In Germany a lawsuit was filed by ex Army Officers and
their families against the Government for exposing them to high levels of
microwaves around radar equipment (an over proportional amount of these soldiers
suffer from certain forms of cancer, many have died already). Animals have been
found to develop brain tumors when exposed to cell phone frequencies at moderate
power levels.
Every day the amount of man made electrosmog increases together with the amount
of RF energy absorbed by human body tissue.
Sure our immune system will do its best to counteract any possible negative
health effects caused by this influx as good as it can. But when would you start
saying enough is enough? And most importantly who should say this? The legions of
dying people well separated from the general public by thick hospital walls - yes
of course, if they could.

leaves a burn mark doesnt eliminate the mark simply because a cause wasnt 
associated. The need for pure, unquestionable logic states that "hey, I got 
burned and it hurts from when I was near that electrical/ hot thing". So 
next time, I stay away from it and ,hey, I dont get burned.Well, all of this 
IS subjective, in a sense,thats what helps to keep our lives and science 
more balanced.What proves to be the truth with any subjective standard, must 
lie within the facts related to the experiance. Do you disqualify the 
elecrtical strike on the TV and radio station in july, in Tennessee?? Prove 
that it wasnt a massive power surge.Or that it wasnt done by the M.I.B. 
Burned birds on the ground, fried electrical components etc, tells me by my 
logic and common sense, that something happened, and I do believe it. But 
just because I cant go the owners or perpetrators of that power surge, and 
ask them to do it again, or just because I cant duplicate that massive use 
of technology within the laboratory, doesnt mean it did not 
happen.Speculative, assumptive, conjecture, ok, so what do I really care 
about that?? All I really care to know is within my self, to my own proof, 
that I may have seen or felt an experiance worth sharing.Proof isnt always 
at the ready hand from a resource station or petrie dish. Most of us have 
experianced a tangible effect which we can verifiably point a finger to and 
say" this is when such,such happened". Explain to me my feeling the power 
force field in the woods that day, tell me about what it COULD have been , 
or tell me what it WASNT.So I'm standing about a 1/4 mile (line of sight) 
from the Navys vlf site up here at Jim Creek, Washington State,and I step 
out of my car, hearing the 2 tones very, very strongly, and then I realize I 
am aslo standing in some sort of magnetic force field, or some sort of 
microwave broadcast, and fel the tingling all over the surface of my body. 
Tell me its impossible to feel something like that. Tell me, with proof and 
with scientifically  verifiable proof,what it feels like to be 
microwaved.Does the scientific community have any survivors who can explain 
to us what that feeling was? I dont think so. So I have no choice but to 
believe by faith, and believe by human understanding and common sense, that 
it was some powerful energy force I was standing in. It is also that human 
understanding of logic and common sense which told  me after I was standing 
there for only a couple of minutes, to "GET OUT OF THERE"!!! And yet, I'm 
still trying to apply your stoic reliance upon the laboratory, to gather 
scientific data, by trying to duplicate that same feeling, by returning to 
the same spot so I may feel that energy force one more time. If I become ill 
or am vaporized, then I will know the scientific method  was right, correct? 
I am not offended by your posture with these methods, as I stated, society 
does need to rely on the scientific approach, to validate certain physical 
phenomanon, but that reliance doesnt keep me imprisoned within those 
constraints. I utilize my intellect and freedom of logic and common sense, 
to fully accept the results of the physical effects of this world upon my 
body and consciousness.

Seriously man, you gotta start using paragraphs.  Our eyes are going buggy 
and I bet a lot of people aren't reading you all the way through. There's a 
reason all books, magazines, and newspapers use paragraphs.  Besides being 
easier to read, it also helps the writer to organize his/her thoughts, with 
each paragraph supposed to represent a new thought. 

<< I am saying, sometimes it takes " going out of 
the box" to get a different or fresher view of the situation. >>

What you mean here isn't clear. If you mean that one can come up with a novel 
theory or hypotheses about something, then I think no one would disagree. But 
if you mean one should use something other than the scientific method to find 
out how things work in the physical world, then you're going to run into 
problems. You will find yourself with no method for resolving contradictions 
or mutually exclusive statements.   

You used the word logic several times. No dispute there. The scientific 
method is nothing if it isn't based on logic. 

Let me use an example from Philosophy of Science 101 that many of us should 
remember.  I think it may be useful in thinking about the hum. 

One of the main things the scientific method seeks to do is to isolate the 
variable.
Say you know nothing about the effects of alcohol.  Then you drink several 
rum and cokes and find yourself drunk on your ass.  At the point you could 
just as easily conclude that it was the coke that was making you drunk. So 
what would you do?
You'd conduct an experiment to try to isolate the variable. You'd drink coke 
and notice that it had no intoxicating effect. Then you'd drink some rum and 
notice that by the 4th glass you're moaning to the fat guy down at the end of 
the bar, "Hey, I love you man."  At the point you could reasonably conclude 
that it was the rum, or something in the rum, that was making you drunk.

Peter Freihofner wrote:

> Hi JConn2299,

> In my area I have met 5 people so far who also can hear/feel a low frequency
> noise at various times.
> Over the past 3 years I did a number of acoustical experiments and came to the
> conclusion that my hum (which might be different to theirs) is not of an acoustic
> nature i.e. is not carried to the ear by sound waves.
> 
> The hum started for me about 10 years ago. Before this time I lived in different
> places 16.000 km away. Today, when I think back, I had never heard hum there. 1.5
> years ago I visited some of these places - still not the slightest hint of a hum
> there.
> In the last 10 years at my present location there were periods which were
> completely hum free. These periods lasted for a few days to several months.
> My hum can vary in intensity. My wife's hum also varies but not necessarily in
> sync with mine.
> 
> I can make my hum louder by certain activities like rushing up and down the
> stairs several times or by exposing myself to low frequency noise (which also
> raises my blood pressure) for a short time after which I hear hum for a few
> minutes at an elevated volume and as a rather constant tone.
> I can also make the hum briefly disappear by certain head movements.
> 
> All the above activities have one thing in common:
> they change certain vital sign parameters like the blood pH value temporarily.
> 
> I also know that the wavelength of induced electromagnetic energy inside any
> living organism is subject to change with blood pH value, salinity of the body
> tissue, temperature etc.
> 
> Certain cell structures inside our bodies absorb externally induced electrical
> energy. The extent of the absorption depends on the wavelength of the applied EM
> energy among other factors.
> If the cell structure happens to be in connection with the auditory and/or
> vestibular system then this induced energy most likely interferes with normal
> signals within the sensoneural paths.
> If the induced electrical energy carries frequency components which are inside
> the tonal range of our hearing then there will most likely be an artificial
> impression of a sound.
> It is quite likely though that a number of closely spaced RF frequencies
> intermodulate inside the sensitive cell structures and produce an audible
> frequency.
> This explains to me why the tone I hear has something of a resonating quality.
> The tones sound like a varying warbling modulation.
> If you had a number of years of experimenting with electronics under your belt
> you would know what I am talking about.
> 
> Now the sensitivity to these hum causing external signals is not the same in
> every organism in that the sensitivity is influenced by so many individual
> factors. The hum causing factors for one person can be either totally different,
> or very similar to another person's set of factors. These factors depend on the
> internal makeup of each specimen. The efficacy of these external triggers are
> just as individually different as the audible impressions caused by these.
> It's a little bit like each of us carrying a fixed tuned radio around. The
> channel each one's radio is tuned at, is totally random but fixed for most of the
> time. Only if a nearby transmitter by coincidence broadcasts on the same channel
> as your radio then you can hear the music.......
>

> is a state of matter.
>

>
> Ether can't be matter, dark or otherwise, or it would interact with
> other matter.  Ether must not do that.
>
> > magnetic-field
>
> Magnetism is a manifestation of one of the four known forces and it
> simply does not have the properties required of ether.  Note that light
> passing through a perfect vacuum is unaffected by magnetic fields of any
> intensity.  Ditto electrostatic fields and other EM waves.  While we're
> at it, gravity is another interaction of matter with other matter so it
> cannot be ether, either.
>

>

> reality?  The trouble is that nothing known has the properties ether
> must possess to do the job it was invented to do.
>

Hey folks,

I think the long hot summer has a few of us getting up on the wrong side of
the bed.  The thing I like about this list is that it has a whole range of
people, all interested in one or several unexplained sounds known
affectionatly as the Taos-Hum.  Some of us have advanced degrees in subjects
that are relevant, some of us are just people that hear the "hum" and are
interested in just what the heck it might be and what it's doing to us,
every one has a valid opinion.  That's what gives this list a special flavor
that one doesnt find on a strictly scientific list.

JConn's comments were valid.  Whether they can be done in the real world or
not.  I'm sure he and every one else here understand though, that there are
people on the list that simply want to express their pain and frustration
and may or may not have the tools to express or test in a scientific manner.
Their opinions and observations are valid as well.  It's odd how some of the
most valuable gems come from the most unlikely places.

The internet is famous for the missunderstandings that it spawns.  I have on
occassion sat in front of my screen with my mouth hanging wide open in
amazement at someone's reaction to something I wrote, wondering just how
they could have missunderstood so completly.  I think of you all as friends
and I really don't want to see anyone get so hurt that they stop posting.

On another subject.  A couple of nights ago the hum was really loud.  So
when I went to bed, I put on a Carlos Nakai CD to go to sleep to.  It had
his flute and a couple of saxaphones on it, Paul Horn was the other artist
as I recall.  The really weird thing, was that when one of the saxaphones
was playing, there was no hum.  It didn't happen with the flute or the
higher pitched sax, just, I think, the alto sax.  I could hear the hum over
all the other music, but when that particular sax was played, the hum
completly went away.  Silence behind the music, it was really neat.

I've always known that there was stress related with the hearing of the hum,
but when that sax played and nulified the hum, I could feel my body relax
and when the sax stopped and the hum returned, my body tensed up again.
Sigh.

Last weekend I was camping with my three nephews at a small lake in the
mountains.  In the evening when the lake had turned into a mirror with not a
ripple on it, my nephews started tossing pebbles and rocks into the lake.
Pretty soon the whole lake was full of little waves, crossing each other,
pushing the waves of one rock further than they would have gone if the rock
behind it hadn't been tossed in, waves filled the lake.

I started wondering if the sound waves around us are similar.  We talk about
turning off this insturment or another in order to test if it is the source
of our hum.  But would that work in this world of sounds every where.  Is
our atmosphere a bit like that lake.  So full of sound waves that turning
off one source would make little difference.  In recent years I have not
been able to find anyplace that I don't hear a hum, some times two or three
different hums.

Consider just the sounds that your house makes.  I live in a rural part of
Oregon where we have occassional power outages.  I love it when the power
goes out.  I can still hear a hum in the distance, but the close in hums of
appliances and electricity cease.  Short of a world wide electrical outage,
I'm not sure that it is possible to turn off enough things for some of us to
not hear a hum.

Just some thoughts, not scientific I know.  You all take care, talk to you
later.

Cathy

Something I have noted... 

If this hum is not recordable i.e. it does not create a vibration in air
then it is not a sound... so then what is it... is it really heard or
just experienced in the head. My experiences are from within and without
and seem like to be centred in the pineal gland. I remember when I was a
child that I used to think I was being followed by a small monitoring
ufo that was just behind my head and I could not see it as it would
always relocate itself as I turned my head... I know that reads as
'looney' but kids come up with the damnest things don't they... I never
could catch it out and it was there for a long time until I reached
puberty and never seemed to come back until I did some serious
meditational practices and lived in the country.

I remember reading somewhere that the pineal gland atrophies and
calcifies? at puberty due to lack of use... this may have been the
source of the change in my perception of it... and may be that the use
of the mushrooms and my meditation practices in my irreverent youth
reactivated the pineal... thus allowing my 'hearing' it again.

Food for thought
Chris

I was wondering the same thing, Anders, and whether anyone was going to
have the nerve to ask. I paid particular attention to my hum yesterday
and found that it contained many more frequencies than are usually
present and it was intense, hard to tune out and probably difficult to
mask (I don't try to mask it any more, so I don't really know). 

I would have posted something myself, but the recent exchange on this
list inhibits any honest exchange, especially about subjective
observations. Many of the truly interesting people on the list have been
pretty silent, and I have stopped looking to the list for any kind of
real information. I only maintain my subscription because I keep
hoping....

But yes, it was different, especially in the early afternoon. I cannot
speak to the morning, as I was running errands and the diesel engine of
my truck overrides any hum that might be present. The hum intensity of
yesterday afternoon occurred after a very quiet day the day before where
the medium frequency hum was faint and the low frequency rumble was
absent. Both (and more) were present yesterday. This morning the hum is
more normal, but still quite intense...unusual for a morning. The rumble
is still present, in itself an oddity, because it has been absent much
of the time in recent months.

It may also be of note that I woke up with a start probably about 5:30
a.m. PDT (8:30 a.m. eastern and probably 1230Z) with a horrific feeling
of stress and anxiety. I got up and tried to walk it off, and went back
to bed, listened to some music, and could not get back to sleep. I could
find no reason for the anxiety, and I do not remember that the hum was
abnormally intense at that particular time. I finally got up, got
dressed and walked out into the hall, turned on a light and looked at my
watch. It was 6 o'clock sharp my time. I did not find out until later in
the day that the time coincided with the beginning of yesterday's
incidents. 

Judy

> On another subject.  A couple of nights ago the hum was really loud.  So
> when I went to bed, I put on a Carlos Nakai CD to go to sleep to.  It had
> his flute and a couple of saxaphones on it, Paul Horn was the other artist
> as I recall.  The really weird thing, was that when one of the saxaphones
> was playing, there was no hum.  It didn't happen with the flute or the
> higher pitched sax, just, I think, the alto sax.  I could hear the hum over
> all the other music, but when that particular sax was played, the hum
> completly went away.  Silence behind the music, it was really neat.
> 
> I've always known that there was stress related with the hearing of the hum,
> but when that sax played and nulified the hum, I could feel my body relax
> and when the sax stopped and the hum returned, my body tensed up again.
> Sigh.
> 
> Last weekend I was camping with my three nephews at a small lake in the
> mountains.  In the evening when the lake had turned into a mirror with not a
> ripple on it, my nephews started tossing pebbles and rocks into the lake.
> Pretty soon the whole lake was full of little waves, crossing each other,
> pushing the waves of one rock further than they would have gone if the rock
> behind it hadn't been tossed in, waves filled the lake.
> 
> I started wondering if the sound waves around us are similar.  We talk about
> turning off this insturment or another in order to test if it is the source
> of our hum.  But would that work in this world of sounds every where.  Is
> our atmosphere a bit like that lake.  So full of sound waves that turning
> off one source would make little difference.  In recent years I have not
> been able to find anyplace that I don't hear a hum, some times two or three
> different hums.
> 
> Consider just the sounds that your house makes.  I live in a rural part of
> Oregon where we have occassional power outages.  I love it when the power
> goes out.  I can still hear a hum in the distance, but the close in hums of
> appliances and electricity cease.  Short of a world wide electrical outage,
> I'm not sure that it is possible to turn off enough things for some of us to
> not hear a hum.
> 
> Just some thoughts, not scientific I know.  You all take care, talk to you
> later.

hi Redphone,
<p>so you think it is man made? So do I most of the time.
<br>If I get a chance I'll try to demodulate the signal below.
<br>But maybe one of you guys has the time to do a quick and dirty mixer
followed by a PLL demodulator.
<br>Such a circuit would be extremely useful if one want's to listen to
navy transmitter music. The signal is pushed out @ 19.8 kHz with a heartwarming
1 megawatt of power.
<br>The modulation scheme is MSK and the side bands stretch out to 70 something
Hz.
<br>If someone wants to do an analysis of the recording, I have it on wav
file.
<br>As I mentioned before I am most interested in demodulating and listening
to this signal to see (hear) if it bears any resemblance to my hum. Your
help would be most appreciated.
<br>And thanks Redphone, for mentioning the title of this HAARP story,
I think I read it in the past.
<br>cheers, Peter.

> Kathy:
>
> You are just fine in your thinking if what we are
> dealing with were just acoustics.  I may be wrong, but I
> think we are being affected by extremely low frequency
> electromagnetic radiation (ELF/EMR).  Sound, accoustic
> energy can be extremely low frequency too.  But it (as
> far as I know) doesn't have a powerful electromagnetic
> component.
>
> Do you think this phenomenon is sound or electromagnetic?
>

I suspect that it may be both.  I think we are being hit by so many
different types of energy and sound waves at various frequencies that it has
become almost impossible to determine where one stops and the next starts,
much less the effect that they have on the human body.

The one thing I know for sure is that I personaly almost never have relief
anymore.  The sound is not always the same, some times it very clearly
modulates, some times not, some times it sounds like it is right outside my
window, other times it sounds as though it is far off in the distance.  Some
times I can distinguish more than one sound.  On occassion I have heard
short bursts of a very high pitched sound that drowns out every thing else.

Most of the time I am able to put it in the background and ignor it, but
some times I will notice that I am really on edge and I'll take a deep
breath, close my eyes and there it will be, kinda like one of those songs on
the radio that you don't notice until some one turns off the radio and you
suddenly find your body relaxing at the relief of the quiet.

There are times that I sense that it isn't sound, but I've never quite known
what it was.  Perhaps, very possibly, electromagnetic pulses.  One of the
reasons that I moved to a rural location is to search for quiet.  Darned if
they didn't put a cell phone tower on a butte not 2 miles away.  Having
consiously noticed a buzz since the late 70's, I can hardly remember what it
was like to not hear it.

I found it interesting recently to find referenced in one of Alex
Constantine's books, newspaper articles from the Oregonian in the mid 70's
verifing that parts of Oregon had been targeted by electromagnetic pulses in
some sort of experiment.  Apparently the only reason it had been covered was
that many thousands of people had become physically ill and they had done
the research to find out why.  If the people hadn't become ill enough for
the newspaper to take note, we probably wouldn't know about the experiment.
Kinda makes you think of the recent events that our fellow list member has
been experiencing.  I do not personally remember reading the articles at the
time, but this is the time period or shortly afterwards when I started
hearing a hum.

Cathy
