Hello All,

This may seem a little outside the current thread of conversation,  but =
I had promised a number of members of this list to post my findings =
resulting from my two month journey to try to escape from the hum.  I =
closed my shop on July 9/01,  and rented out my house so I could devote =
8 weeks to travel,  camping all the way,  through the remotest country =
accessible by two wheel drive.  My aim was to determine two basic =
factors:

a:  Is the hum a local phenomenon,  present in some areas but not in =
others.

b:  Is the hum a characteristic of proximity to civilization,  and/or =
industry.

My route went from Vancouver Island east across BC,  into Alberta via =
the Crowsnest Pass,  then north through Calgary to Slave Lake,  then =
west through Grande Prairie to the start of the Alaska Highway,  north =
on that to Whitehorse,  and onto the Klondike Highway to Dawson City in =
the Yukon,  then to Carcross and to Skagway in Alaska,  then a dip into =
BC to the Atlin district,  and finally east to Watson Lake to take the =
Stewart-Cassiar road south through BC and the Duffy Lake road to the =
coast.  I have listed the major towns along the way as recognizable =
waypoints,  although I avoided them for camping,  choosing old unused =
mining or logging roads to access wilderness settings as far from =
settlements as I could get.  I needed quiet environments where the hum,  =
if present,  would be clearly noticeable.  I covered a total of 6,250 =
statute miles start to finish. =20

The places where I heard the hum,  in addition to Vancouver Is.  were;  =
Calgary,  Dawson City,  the Atlin District,  and 100 Mile House in the =
Southern Caribou.  The one thing that all these places had in common =
were that they were the only places where I stayed more than two days.  =
In other words,  as long as I stayed on the move daily I experienced no =
hum.  In every place where I stayed more than two days,  on the morning =
of the third day the hum would be there. Calgary was the only city that =
I stayed in,  because I have two sons that live and work there,  so a =
visit was in order.  On the third day the hum was unmistakable.  In =
every place that I heard the hum,  it was exactly the same as the so =
familiar one back home.

One night,  near Slave Lake in Alberta,  I chose a camp late at night,  =
very tired.  In the morning I was surprised to discover that I was =
practically on top of a high-pressure natural gas pipeline.  I had slept =
like a babe,  and heard no hum.  So much for the pipeline theory.  =
Underway that morning,  I chose a more attractive site a little further =
on to cook some breakfast,  and became aware of a sort of hum,  not =
quite like the usual.  About a quarter of a mile further on the source =
revealed itself as a pumping station for that same pipeline.  I passed =
it and about a mile beyond stopped once more,  turning off the engine =
and listening very intently,  heard nothing.  So although the pumping =
stations do give off acoustic VLF's,  they do not travel particularly =
far. =20

Another seemingly bad choice of camp was in the Caribou district when =
dawn revealed high-tension power lines nearby.  I hadn't seen them in =
the dark,  and although I did not sleep well I did not hear any hum. =20

Cell phones do not work at all throughout most of the north country,  I =
checked mine frequently to find no signal in any of the places I camped =
in northern BC and the Yukon.

I heard the hum clearly on the Juneau Icefield,  on the Atlin district =
side known as the Llewellyn Glacier.   Here there is no cell tower,  =
pipeline,  power line,  or any mining,  logging,  or industrial =
activity.  The nearest civilization is Juneau,  60 miles away on the =
other side of the Coast Mountains.  I had been exploring the vast south =
end of Atlin Lake by kayak and so was in the area long enough for the =
hum to start,  as usual,  on the third day.  It seemed very loud in that =
otherwise intensely quiet place. =20

Based on my experiences,  here are a few tentative conclusions I have =
come to:

1.  The hum is general in the environment,  and global in scale.  ELF =
EMR circles the globe with extremely little energy loss,  so proximity =
to any source is not a factor.  There is no escape,  except perhaps in =
terms of countermeasures.=20

2.  Entrainment to these signals is a function of duration of exposure =
as well as nervous system condition.  It appears that =
time/motion/distance interrupts the entrainment temporarily,  which =
reasserts,  in my case,  on the third day of not covering distance.  =20

3.  Being in civilization or far from it makes no difference.

4.  Judging by the descriptions posted by some contributors,  it seems =
we are not all experiencing the same thing.  There appear to be three =
broad categories of hum:

        a:  the constant,  idling diesel EM type that is everywhere and =
lacking directionality
        b:  acoustic pollution from nearby industry,  which is local and =
has directionality
        c:  internal causes

The difficulty is that any of the above would be very difficult to =
prove/disprove by any scientific method.  Local industrial noise of =
course could be recorded,  but doesn't explain a loud hum on the Juneau =
Icefield for instance which most likely could not be recorded by any =
audio equipment.  Many hum sufferers have been to hearing specialists =
with inconclusive results and no solutions,  so internal causes also =
would be hard to confirm/deny. =20

I no longer believe it is directed,  but rather just random EM =
pollution.  I liked Cathy Pritchett's analogy of the ripples on the =
lake...but instead of picturing sound waves,  imagine the outwardly =
emanating concentric circles to be radio energy from countless =
transmitters and the interference patterns where they cross each other =
may be part of the hum.  I also still consider the Loran-C system as a =
possible culprit,  along with ELF sub coms and other Military =
communications. =20

I apologize for this rather lengthy post but I went a long way outside =
of my ordinary routine to make this long distance experiment and I hope =
some of these observations may prove to shed a little more light on a =
complex problem. =20

Regards,

Alf Bangert




   =20

Alf,
Did you notice any other vehicles that appeared within 2 miles of where you 
were located when the hum became present after remaining there over two days?
I state this as my own experiences have been that the hum seems to be 
present, when the certain individuals show up in the area. Meaning that the 
device is portable and used for purposeful, intentional and continual 
harassment. 
I suggest monitoring the presence of others who coincidentally "show up" in 
the area you dwell for more than two days. It would also help to maintain a 
journal of the presence of these individuals, time date place license plates 
and descriptions...as well as taking pictures or carry a camcorder for 
evidence.
This continual harassment of certain targeted individuals in the United 
States is not simply happenstance. 

Vicki Carlson

>From: "Alf Bangert" <alfbangert@telus.net>
>Reply-To: taoshum-l@eskimo.com
>To: <taoshum-l@eskimo.com>
>Subject: Some observations
>Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2001 00:31:22 -0700
>
>Hello All,
>
>This may seem a little outside the current thread of conversation,  but I 
>had promised a number of members of this list to post my findings resulting 
>from my two month journey to try to escape from the hum.  I closed my shop 
>on July 9/01,  and rented out my house so I could devote 8 weeks to travel, 
>  camping all the way,  through the remotest country accessible by two 
>wheel drive.  My aim was to determine two basic factors:
>
>a:  Is the hum a local phenomenon,  present in some areas but not in 
>others.
>
>b:  Is the hum a characteristic of proximity to civilization,  and/or 
>industry.
>
>My route went from Vancouver Island east across BC,  into Alberta via the 
>Crowsnest Pass,  then north through Calgary to Slave Lake,  then west 
>through Grande Prairie to the start of the Alaska Highway,  north on that 
>to Whitehorse,  and onto the Klondike Highway to Dawson City in the Yukon,  
>then to Carcross and to Skagway in Alaska,  then a dip into BC to the Atlin 
>district,  and finally east to Watson Lake to take the Stewart-Cassiar road 
>south through BC and the Duffy Lake road to the coast.  I have listed the 
>major towns along the way as recognizable waypoints,  although I avoided 
>them for camping,  choosing old unused mining or logging roads to access 
>wilderness settings as far from settlements as I could get.  I needed quiet 
>environments where the hum,  if present,  would be clearly noticeable.  I 
>covered a total of 6,250 statute miles start to finish.
>
>The places where I heard the hum,  in addition to Vancouver Is.  were;  
>Calgary,  Dawson City,  the Atlin District,  and 100 Mile House in the 
>Southern Caribou.  The one thing that all these places had in common were 
>that they were the only places where I stayed more than two days.  In other 
>words,  as long as I stayed on the move daily I experienced no hum.  In 
>every place where I stayed more than two days,  on the morning of the third 
>day the hum would be there. Calgary was the only city that I stayed in,  
>because I have two sons that live and work there,  so a visit was in order. 
>  On the third day the hum was unmistakable.  In every place that I heard 
>the hum,  it was exactly the same as the so familiar one back home.
>
>One night,  near Slave Lake in Alberta,  I chose a camp late at night,  
>very tired.  In the morning I was surprised to discover that I was 
>practically on top of a high-pressure natural gas pipeline.  I had slept 
>like a babe,  and heard no hum.  So much for the pipeline theory.  Underway 
>that morning,  I chose a more attractive site a little further on to cook 
>some breakfast,  and became aware of a sort of hum,  not quite like the 
>usual.  About a quarter of a mile further on the source revealed itself as 
>a pumping station for that same pipeline.  I passed it and about a mile 
>beyond stopped once more,  turning off the engine and listening very 
>intently,  heard nothing.  So although the pumping stations do give off 
>acoustic VLF's,  they do not travel particularly far.
>
>Another seemingly bad choice of camp was in the Caribou district when dawn 
>revealed high-tension power lines nearby.  I hadn't seen them in the dark,  
>and although I did not sleep well I did not hear any hum.
>
>Cell phones do not work at all throughout most of the north country,  I 
>checked mine frequently to find no signal in any of the places I camped in 
>northern BC and the Yukon.
>
>I heard the hum clearly on the Juneau Icefield,  on the Atlin district side 
>known as the Llewellyn Glacier.   Here there is no cell tower,  pipeline,  
>power line,  or any mining,  logging,  or industrial activity.  The nearest 
>civilization is Juneau,  60 miles away on the other side of the Coast 
>Mountains.  I had been exploring the vast south end of Atlin Lake by kayak 
>and so was in the area long enough for the hum to start,  as usual,  on the 
>third day.  It seemed very loud in that otherwise intensely quiet place.
>
>Based on my experiences,  here are a few tentative conclusions I have come 
>to:
>
>1.  The hum is general in the environment,  and global in scale.  ELF EMR 
>circles the globe with extremely little energy loss,  so proximity to any 
>source is not a factor.  There is no escape,  except perhaps in terms of 
>countermeasures.
>
>2.  Entrainment to these signals is a function of duration of exposure as 
>well as nervous system condition.  It appears that time/motion/distance 
>interrupts the entrainment temporarily,  which reasserts,  in my case,  on 
>the third day of not covering distance.
>
>3.  Being in civilization or far from it makes no difference.
>
>4.  Judging by the descriptions posted by some contributors,  it seems we 
>are not all experiencing the same thing.  There appear to be three broad 
>categories of hum:
>
>         a:  the constant,  idling diesel EM type that is everywhere and 
>lacking directionality
>         b:  acoustic pollution from nearby industry,  which is local and 
>has directionality
>         c:  internal causes
>
>The difficulty is that any of the above would be very difficult to 
>prove/disprove by any scientific method.  Local industrial noise of course 
>could be recorded,  but doesn't explain a loud hum on the Juneau Icefield 
>for instance which most likely could not be recorded by any audio 
>equipment.  Many hum sufferers have been to hearing specialists with 
>inconclusive results and no solutions,  so internal causes also would be 
>hard to confirm/deny.
>
>I no longer believe it is directed,  but rather just random EM pollution.  
>I liked Cathy Pritchett's analogy of the ripples on the lake...but instead 
>of picturing sound waves,  imagine the outwardly emanating concentric 
>circles to be radio energy from countless transmitters and the interference 
>patterns where they cross each other may be part of the hum.  I also still 
>consider the Loran-C system as a possible culprit,  along with ELF sub coms 
>and other Military communications.
>
>I apologize for this rather lengthy post but I went a long way outside of 
>my ordinary routine to make this long distance experiment and I hope some 
>of these observations may prove to shed a little more light on a complex 
>problem.
>
>Regards,
>
>Alf Bangert
>

Hi Vicki,

tracking methods to reveal a tail but apparently this was not a factor.  =

surveillance and I really don't think I am that important!  Also,  when =
the hum started at the Llewellyn Glacier,  I was on the far side of =
Atlin Lake,  which is 80 miles long and the nearest "road" was 25 miles =
to the north of where I was on the opposite side of the lake.  I saw no =
other boats for the 4 days I was over there.  The only way to the =
glacier is by helicopter or by boat.  I saw no one at all,  for that =
matter.  I can't imagine any portable device with enough power to reach =
where I was.  That is why I now believe the hum to be general and not =
directed.  You can only discover this,  of course,  by going to places =
where being followed is just about impossible.

I don't know if this is good news or bad,  but it does narrow things =
down a tad.

My experiences have been a bit different in relation to the hum being in all 
and every place.  Generally, most of my travel plans are known prior to 
reaching my locations.  The hum/frequency doesn' t often appear until two 
incidents occur.  1) Occurrence on electrical power lines outside, leading 
into the facility or my home and 2) aircraft in the area.  If my location 
isn't known prior to my arriving at my destination, it takes the 
hum/frequency hours to days to begin. If known ahead of time; it appears when 
I arrive or awaiting me.   I can definitely tell when it's not present.  
Sometimes I can hear the aircraft arriving, other times, only the hovering 
and idling, which appears to open a direct line, path, or window from the 
aircraft into my home.  I've tested the theory by simply going to my door, 
opening it, and sticking my head outside.  When my head is outside, quiet as 
a pin.  When I withdraw my head inside, the hovering and idling sound is 
strong and audible on the inside.

No one can tell me at this point, the reason my smoke detector sounded as if 
data from a fax machine was being transmitted through it, while 
intermittently giving off loud, piercing, long signals.  Last week, I picked 
up a radio station from out west on my AM Radio, after aircraft hovered and 
apparently cleared almost all AM Stations to receive very clear reception.  
The unusual thing:  I turned on another radio, moved to another location in 
my home, and after obtaining no reception at first(but loud signals, moaning, 
etc., I finally picked up stations and they were entirely different from what 
was playing on the AM Stations in the other room, even though they were on 
the same station.

Dorothy

hi all,

i too have experienced a break from the hum after
traveling and then returning.
i have attributed this to the traveling having some
sort of effect on the body and desensitising it for a
time. similar to those people who suffer from a
disturbance to the inner ear causing sickness and
dizziness when traveling.

this effect only occurs for me after long tiring
trips.  when i commute between adelaide and york
peninsula (about 180km) in about two and a half hours,
the hum is already waiting for me.

for the record; i have heard the hum in areas of
inland australia where there is NO power and nearly no
aircraft.

derek

Hello all,

The above link leads to an interesting and thought provoking site.  =
There is some good information there but I am highly doubtful about the =
author's conclusions.  Although I can easily believe that the resonant =
frequency of our planet has been slightly altered by our enthusiastic =
use of electricity and radio frequency communications of all sorts,  I =
would question the sensibility of suggesting that this change in our =
earth's "heartbeat" could possibly be beneficial to our health or =
spiritual well being in any way.  This line of thinking is naive at best =
and possibly downright dangerous as it provides the mechanism for =
passive acceptance of a serious pollutant.  I do not know of any other =
recognized environmental pollutant that has serendipitously provided an =
unexpected health bonus for any living thing.  I fail to see why EM =
pollution should be any different.  But the authors have a book to sell, =
 and therein lies the clue.  We will have,  on a regular basis,  curious =
and unlikely explanations of the hum from those who somehow hope to gain =
notoriety, money,  or a place in history perhaps by dangling before us =
some panacea or placebo to either cure us or make us feel fortunate to =
have a hum.  Cyber snake-oil salesmen.

If the increased frequency of the Schumann resonance is supposed to =
engender an increase in consciousness;  to cause certain individuals to =
evolve to "the next level",  then it is interesting to note that most =
hum sufferers report insomnia,  chronic fatigue,  inability to make =
decisions,  depression,  and even paranoia as a direct result of =
exposure to this hum along with a host of physical symptoms,  none of =
which are positive in nature,  then it becomes almost sinister when some =
suggest this is actually good for us!  Are there any list members out =
there who enjoy the hum?  Have any of you developed heightened spiritual =
states as a result?  (I mean other than those with something to sell!) =20

World events themselves hardly suggest an overall increase in =
consciousness or spirituality.  It beats me on what those childlike =
concepts are based other than,  very loosely,  ancient predictions of =
dubious interpretation.=20

Well,  there is my dubious interpretation for the day!

Cheers,

-Alf Bangert

>From the Society of Amateur Scientists

In the wake of the terrible tragedy in New York on September 11, 2001 a lot 
of us have been wondering what we can do to assist the effort to protect the 
United States from future terrorist attacks. As I write this the death toll 
is unknown, but it will no doubt be many thousands, probably many times more 
than the 2,400 souls lost on December 7, 1941. And as our nation launches a 
sustained effort against international terrorism, it seems quite likely that 
we will see more suicide bombings or perhaps worse, that will kill more 
Americans. My own view is that we are in for a rough decade.


Most of us cannot help directly in the effort to hunt down and destroy the 
perpetrators of the horrible attack on the World Trade Center . However, the 
Society for Amateur Scientists might be able to help mitigate the carnage 
our nation will experience as the war against terrorism escalates to new 
levels. Here's why.


Apparently, the idea of hijacking fully fueled airplanes and crashing them 
into vital US targets was first seriously proposed by novelist Tom Clancy. 
Clancy says that he told a key anti-terrorist person in the military about 
the plot of a book he was writing in which a hijacked plane was deliberately 
crashed into the capital building during a joint session of Congress. He 
asked if the military had thought about this scenario. The analyst, Clancy 
reports, said "No. But I promise you on Monday we will." The terrorists used 
a low tech, relatively low cost tactic that delivered an enormous about of 
energy with high accuracy to high value targets. Their idea was anticipated 
by an amateur analyst.


There's a reason for that. Amateurs are accustomed to thinking up low tech 
solutions to difficult technical problems.

Join the SAS Shadow Team

In security circles, the game of pretending you are the enemy can yield 
tremendous insights into your vulnerabilities. It used to be called Red 
Teaming for obvious Cold War reasons. Today, with the new security 
challenges, it needs a new name. Sheldon Greaves suggests we call the game 
of getting into the terrorist's mind "Shadow Teaming." And that's what we're 
going to call it.


Over the years I've occasionally indulged in Shadow Teaming by trying to 
dream up terrible things I could do if I were a terrorist. First I assume 
only inexpensive methods, and restrict myself to no more technology than I 
could buy at Radio Shack. Then I assume that I am an isolated person or a 
small cell of dedicated terrorists. Further, I assume the terrorists all 
want to survive the attack. (Like the kamikaze of World War II, a suicide 
bomber can inflect a lot of damage. Once. If the US can destroy the camps in 
which these people are trained and financed then the suicide bombers will, 
like the kamikaze, burn themselves out. Personally, I'm much more worried 
about people may be already in this country and who choose to survive to 
attack again.) I've been able to dream up an absolutely frightening array 
ways to very dramatically strike at the infrastructure that we all rely on. 
And in all my schemes the terrorist would survive to attack another day.

My own view is that we will begin to see well-educated terrorists looking 
for ways to do maximum damage and survive. We must not assume that the FBI 
will identify these threats by themselves. We know the technology, and we 
have the expertise to make a real contribution. And I believe it is our duty 
as citizens to contribute that expertise to those who might be able to apply 
it to save American lives.


This is where I believe the Society for Amateur Scientists can make an 
important contribution to our nation's security.


I hope you feel the same way. So I've just created the SAS Anti-Terrorist 
Network to give you a chance to apply your creative energies to protecting 
America. Here's how it works. Dream up your most devious terrorist plots and 
email them to SAS Headquarters. I will put together a panel of experts to 
review all the material we receive and once each quarter we will assemble 
all of the technically feasible ideas into a secret report that we will 
deliver to the FBI. This material will never be published or made available 
to the public or even to the rest of the membership. After all, we don't 
want to train terrorists.


Our community has a great deal to contribute. Please help.


Submissions

Here's a link to some great information about terrorists.

Remember, a terrorist doesn't have to kill people. The aim of political 
terror is to make people feel unsafe. A terrorist can strike at any soft 
target, not necessarily large groups of people. Think about the entire 
infrastructure of the US.

Because SAS does not have a lot of resources to throw at this project, you 
have to do the feasibility analysis yourself. Think the problem through. For 
example, don't just say "poison the water supply." You've got to specify 
exactly which poison, calculate how much they'd need to do the job, explain 
how the terrorists would get it and how they would inject it into a given 
water supply, etc. Don't assume the terrorists have access to any technology 
that you don't have access to.


Apart from that, no rules. Come one everybody, scare me!


Send your submissions ATN@sas.org


I've started a discussion about the Anti-Terrorist Network on the Forum. DO 
NOT DISCUSS SPECIFIC TACTICS IN THE FORUM! The area is reserved to talk 
about what you think about SAS carrying creating the Anti-Terrorist Network, 
and that affects you think it will have if any.


Shawn Carlson
Executive Director

This is nonsense. There is no increase in the Schumman resonance, as is
clearly obvoius at the Data Archive for Magnetic Activity and Schumann
Resonance, http://quake.geo.berkeley.edu/ncedc/em.intro.html.

The authors, who obviously lack basic knowledge of physics, don't understand
harmonic frequencies (14 Hz, etc), as explained at
http://www-star.stanford.edu/~mfuelle/eicr.html.

This silly idea comes from the idiotic book by Braden, Awakening to Zero
Point.

West and others,

The suggestion that the Schumann Resonances are related to the Taos Hum was 
published a short time ago in an article I wrote (Germine, M., 2001.World 
Futures, v. 57, pp. 263-267), which is available from the publisher, Harvard 
Academic Publishers.  
The brain produces ELF electromagnetic radiation, which has been measured 
outside of the head, in the same frequencies as those seen on the EEG.  As we 
know, these low frequency waves, although of very low energy, effect the 
brain through the quantum Stark effect, and are able to create observable 
brain changes, as observed by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (MRI).  The Schumann 
Resonances have a major frequency of about 8 Hz., which corresponds to the 
alpha rhythm of the brain.  Using EMFs of this frequency, I have 
experimentally produced a hum in my own auditory system.  The hum persists 
for some time after EMF exposure, and amplified similar frequency sounds, 
such as airplane engines and fans.  I was sensitized, and heard hums for 
quite some time after the experiments.

The proposition I make in my article is that the low frequency EMFs of the 
brain serve a purpose in the uniting of brain function into a single 
framework in perception and in memory.  They are the only "signals" within 
the brain that could bring about the instantaneous unity of perception we 
observe in consciousness.  They are also the only signals which might be 
transmitted from one brain to another.

Given the possibility that the Shumann resonances are responsible for the 
Taos hum. a whole host of other variable would be involved in subjective 
auditory experience of the hum.  One would the focus of individual attention, 
another the state of activation of the brain, another the possible 
reinforcement of similar waves in the brain, another the state of the 
observing population.

I always get miffed when someone claiming to have expertise uses such 
expertise as an argument for or against a point.  I wonder if West 
understands human physiology, the theory of organic systems, etc., which are 
all involved in the hum, whatever its origin be.  These aspects of the 
problem go far beyond the "basic physics" that West naively and concretely 
identifies with a subjective experience. Certainly, the WTC disaster, 
indirectly, altered the physiological brain state of the population.


Mark Germine, MD, MS, DABPN

symptoms. Yet the most common thread connecting all of us, is the fact that

Rick.

officials and if it's a military operation, contact them too and complain 
that it is an environmental and health violation.  Get ahold of the Greens in 
your area and get them on the bandwagon and all other groups that work in the 
publics' interest.  College professors, school principles, etc.
I first heard the hum in '69 when the Navy began ELF transmissions out of 
northern Michigan.  I remember asking my dad if he heard it too.  He did, but 
like most people we know, he ignored it.  He thought it might be the sawmill 
that was about a quarter mile away.  I walked down there at 3am and the place 
was closed.  There was no talk locally about the technology and I forgot 
about it when I moved out of that small quiet town in '71 and never thought 
about it again until I moved to a rural spot north of L.A. for the quiet.  
I've been listening to it now for three years.  When I read here about that 
ELF transmitter in '69 in upper Michigan, I was satisfied that I was hearing 
ELF. 
Between 71 and 74 we worked hard to stop the war machine and we won.  It can 
still be done.  It takes a lot of sacrifice, but if it bothers you enough, 
you will sacrifice willingly.
I'm thirty miles south of Edward's AFB where much super secret stuff goes 
down.  The hum is coming from the north, but I can't get close enough to 
determine the source.  Given the long distance which this broadcast travels, 
the hum I hear could be produced at the same source you've identified.  So 
make them stop, please.

In a message dated 9/21/01 11:02:20 AM Eastern Daylight Time, 
arider2@hotmail.com writes:

<< The scope of applying the scientific approach is necessary in 
 establishing the first line of study, like a stepping stone to work from, 
 then from there we search to find other appropriate response. >>

No, the scientific method is necessary to establish a conclusion.  You can 
have a working hypothesis, but until you've gathered sufficient evidence, 
isolated the variable, etc.,  you can never state it with any certainty.

And just to throw this in for good measure, a correlation doesn't necessarily 
establish a cause and effect relationship.  This is the classic 
misrepresentation which often occurs when the news media reports on 
scientific studies.  The headline screams something such as, "Coffee Drinkers 
Have A Higher Rate of Cancer,"  and many people jump to the conclusion that 
coffee causes cancer.  Well, that may, or may not,  be the case. There are 
often many variables at play.   I'm just making this up as an example, but it 
may be that coffee drinkers are also more likely to be smokers, and it's the 
smoking that's actually causing the higher cancer rate, not the coffee. 

Same thing with the hum.  Most of the sufferers on this list seem to be 
middle aged.  Does that mean being middle aged causes the hum?   Not 
necessarily, but when you see a correlation such as that, it can mean that it 
might be a fruitful area for investigation.

Hi JCONN, I view the scientific approach more as working toward the end, 
rather that being able to draw a conclusion. But what happens when at that 
point, a conclusion cant be drawn?? Thats when I submit, would be the time 
to interject some remaining data...to fill in the gaps.ie. personal 
testamony, physical symptoms , other data which each of us, for example, can 
contribute to the general cause, at least in this case with this hum/Tone 
phenomanon.What if we as civilians dont have available to us, the proper 
technical equipment to complete the scientific approach... this might only 
delay any conclusions. Sometimes its necessary to somehow( as we've talked 
about in earlier letters)fill in the gaps, not by pure quessing, but by 
process of elimination, collected facts to that point,personal testamony, 
etc. A cause and effect relationship sometimes isnt that finite a process. 
Some intelligent guesswork has to be applied also,as another method,to fill 
in the gaps. If I try to trouble-shoot a certain piece of equipment, the 
style of failure may be caused by a few different reasons or components, but 
the failure looks the same. I might not be able to prove which one was 
responsible, not until I locate and isolate each component. But in the 
interum, I can, by experiance and knowledge, "guess" which one is 
responsible. It fills in the gap until proof can be obtained. In this case, 
we cantr go to the government or military and ask them yto prove the 
technology for us, so we are stuck with more archaic methods until a more 
apropriate instrument can be obtained. Loke for example, the idea is good 
but cant be proven until technology catches up with the idea, or invention. 
Anyway, thanks for your insight. Have a good day. Rick

Rick,
Of course the US needs a military defense, but when the technologies employed 
to monitor the air and sea are also invasive of its citizens, as is the case 
with ELF etc., then we have to rethink the strategy.  I'm opposed to covering 
up the sound with a neutralizer as this can't be universally applied and only 
adds more noise to the environment.  A passive technology is the only way out 
of this.  Meanwhile, I, again, resent that I am being attacked by this sound 
24/7 and can't even move anywhere to escape it.  I'm sure they plan to use 
this tech in star wars too.  Is nuclear weapons in space cool with you too?  
Do you think spending 30 cents on the tax dollar for defense is wise when we 
can already blow up the world ten times over?  I'm not angry with men and 
women who choose to serve in the military, but I am angry with the techno and 
military industrialists who rep outrageous profits from these products at our 
expense and sell war worldwide, when they could be making things which 
benefit mankind.  Yes, this country's got it over most places on earth, well 
then shouldn't we be exporting peace and prosperity rather than watching our 
own quality of life go down to meet the third worlds' standard?

Tom    

Tom

In the never ending debate over whether the Hum is most probably caused 
by EM radiation -- in most models supposed to directly influence the 
auditory apparatus/brain --, an acoustic vibration in the Earth -- which 
consequently must be caused by something else, a man-made or a natural 
phenomenon, vibrating inside the earth -- or is an altogether internal 
sensation, with or without an external trigger, there is one possibility 
which has been constantly overlooked: that the Hum is caused by some kind 
of gravity wave or similar physical phenomenon.

There are in fact observations which could sustain a 'gravity wave 
hypothesis'. Dr. Franz from Germany wrote the following:

>>>

Subject: 
               German Hum 
     Date: 
               Tue, 6 Mar 2001 22:07:19 +0100 
   From: 
               Frosch.Com@t-online.de (frosch)
        To: 
               taoshum-l@eskimo.com


<snip>

Several persons of this list already found out, that HUM is NOT of acoustic 
and NOT of electromagnetic origin. If one does not trust them, he/she 
easily can repeat the studies, she/he only have to invest tens of thousands 
of Euro`s or $ to repeat the studies, which already have been done. I myself 
spent this money, because I did not know these studies at that time; and I 
have to confirm the results: HUM is not of direct acoustic and not of acute 
electromagnetic origin. If one wants to repeat these studies, I can give 
recomendatios for the experiments.

I did buy expensive Mu-Metal and Cu- shieldings against all kind of EM-
waves as well as sensitive microphones to finally realize that I do hear a 
sound that is not existant externally and does not have an electromagnetic 
counterpart!! This was a sad experience.

<<<

What Dr. Fritz' final interpretation of these experiments were and what his 
current Hum hypothesis is, is not known to the Taoshum-L since Dr. Fritz 
-- possibly in dismay of the frustrating terms of a serious debate on this 
forum -- evidently signed off soon after the message above.

Still, Dr. Fritz' independent confirmation of the observation, previously 
made by the University of NM study, that the Hum can still be heard inside 
a 'Faraday's Cage' constructed according to the modern 'scientific' 
standard: -> an observation which rules out the hypothesis that the cause 
of the Hum could be EM radiation of any frequency.

Several people (including myself once, see the message vault) have tried to 
apply Occams Razor to carve out a piece of meat, but if this philosophical 
tool for cutting out BS is interpreted to mean that the Hum should and 
could _only_ be explained by categories which are _already_ explained (for 
example according to schoolbook physics), then we might be in for a 
_never_ ending discussion if the Hum is a yet not explained and fully 
understood phenomenon. Which seems to be the case.

If this is indeed the case, it seems especially important to explore all 
possible hypotheses and not to loose track with observed Hum 
phenomenology.

EM radiation cannot penetrate a 'Faraday's Box', but a gravity wave 
certainly could.

A gravity wave would further vibrate all matter it passes and would 
therefor be indistinguishable from an acoustical wave; -> at least as 
'heard' by a transducer, be it a microphone, a hydrophone, a geophone or an 
ear.

A gravity wave would vibrate _all_ matter it passes, thereby creating that 
aerie omnipresent character of the Hum. If the Hum vibration was only 
present in solid earth, the impedance mismatch at the earth/air boundary 
would make it virtually impossible to hear/record the Hum in air. A gravity 
wave would however vibrate the matter of the air the same way as 'solid' 
matter.

The source of a gravity wave responsible for the Hum would be virtually 
impossible to determine; -> it could be coming from the center of our 
galaxy or from some kind of secret experiment or technology on earth. The 
source might even be some kind of resonance in the spherical capacitor 
formed by the earth-ionosphere-cavity (where also the Shumann resonance 
rings). There is a considerable tension between Heaven and Earth, enough to 
jolt the electro-gravity effects into motion.

For a primer in electro-gravitics, see http://soteria.com/brown/main.htm

               

                    Friendly greetings from humming Hunneberg: $£

Hi Stefan,

your gravity/hum hypothesis is interesting.

But please do not rule out the EM/hum hypothesis as yet which I believe
you are
doing when you say:
***************************
Still, Dr. Fritz' independent confirmation of the observation,
previously
made by the University of NM study, that the Hum can still be heard
inside
a 'Faraday's Cage' constructed according to the modern 'scientific'
standard: -> an observation which rules out the hypothesis that the
cause
of the Hum could be EM radiation of any frequency.
***************************

as a reminder, this is what Dr. Frosch wrote about his own EM
experiments:
***************************
Dear all,
I built a copper chamber of 2m*1m*1m with 1 mm copper sheets with
absolute no
openings. Inside I measured an attenuation of the magnetic field
compared to
outside as follows:
50 Hz: -14 dB
150 Hz: -20 dB
250 Hz: -24 dB
Even with an additional Mu-metal cylinder (220 cm diameter 35 cm height
2 mm
diameter) over the head I could not get to stop humming.
My conclusion is that there cannot be an acute influence of  alternating

electromagnetic fields. About chronic, sensitizing effects which cannot
be ruled

out this test does not give an answer.
Regards
Franz
****************************

Now Stefan, you see how inefficient the shielding of his cage is in the
low
frequency range? -14 db @ 50 Hz and worse at lower frequencies.
This is peanuts not shielding.
At best I would call his cage an attenuator but not a shield.
Secondly, Dr. Frosch tells us that his test cannot rule out long term
sensitization which may or may not have been caused by EM.
So in a nutshell Dr. Frosch' experiments cannot be used as an argument
against
the EM/hum hypothesis.

Just a side note: commercial shielded rooms employ several layers of
different
kinds of metals, amounting up to centimetres of thickness in order to
achieve a
relatively field free environment.
Instead of spending tens of grands on (unfortunatley still inferior)
shielding
materials, I'd make an appointment with one of the manufacturers of
these rooms
and ask for permission to sit in one of these for a few hours.......

cheers, Peter.
BTW did your spell checker also have difficulties with the word Frosch?
....
your own name always comes out as "Sean" on mine ;-)

Dorothy,

What I meant by the last message was that you are hearing ordinary powerline 
noise which doesn't travel very far.  If you go in the very near vicinity of 
huge power lines you can hear them sing and they'll even make your hair stand 
on end and I know a guy who sticks metal rods in the ground and powers small 
devices.  But this is not the Hum which we and the Taos folks are listening 
to.  The Hum travels long distances, I mean thousands of miles.  Your power 
lines won't be heard a quarter mile away.  If you hear a hum when you're not 
in the vicinity of power lines, then you're hearing the Hum we're talking 
about.  I would suggest you move away form the power lines, but then you'd 
probably hear the big Hum, and I don't want to be responsible for anyone 
hearing that.

Tom

As you can see from the dates of the papers by TT Brown and the 'Biefield-
Brown-Effect' (the link I supplied) it is possible/probable that secret 
research programs on electro-gravity (and similar phenomena) were 
initiated as early as the middle 'fifties. If this kind of research has made 
any spectacular break-throughs, they are most probably classified.

>Are gravity waves a recent invention then?

While you look at a star, it can suddenly (always 'suddenly') turn into a 
nova/supernova. Sometimes whole galaxies light up...about the same time 
as a storm of cosmic radiation reaches and scorches the observer into 
oblivion. Perhaps the gravity wave from this event -- if gravity waves 
have superluminal speed -- reached and _almost_ erased life on this 
hypothetical observer's home planet eons _earlier_ in time. Nothing is 
perfectly safe. Presently the geomagnetic field is rapidly getting weaker. 
During pre-historic cataclysmic events, associated with mass extinction 
of whole species, the geomagnetic field has been several orders of 
magnitude more intense. The universe has no 'steady state', at least not in 
our time scale.

_Inside_ our time scale 'the space weather' is also constantly shifting.

Hi Bob -

I used to teach Biology, Chemistry, and Physics in High School. I often had
religious material and tracts given to me for teaching any form of natural
selection, let alone corrupted misunderstandings of Darwin's work.  This was
often done by the fundamentalist press. Unfortunately, the quality of
textbooks and education in general has been on the decline for many years
now in the United States.

Judeo-Christian scripture states that man was created from the "dust of the
Earth" - atoms and molecules- but doesn't say how, and that "God breathed
into man the breath of life, and he became a living Soul." The words for
breath in a number of languages may also be translated "Spirit."  Also
nobody has ever found "The Missing Link" of false Darwinism, because there
never was one!

I believe, and I am an ordained minister, that when the physical structure
of what became man "evolved" to a certain level, that being became capable
of housing an individual Spirit or Soul,
one entered into him.  Now, I also believe that all of Creation is made from
the essence of what many call God, therefore everything is Holy. That's why
I believe it would be beneficial for everyone to at least study Taoism,
Buddhism, and Native American Spirituality; none of them has this problem.

It's very unfortunate that Science and Religions fight over a subject where
there is no real conflict if everything were properly understood. Many
people who write textbooks for children over simplify, and probably have
only studied in a narrow-minded fashion themselves.

Thanks for your response.
Love and Light,
John Spiritwalker

S. Loftsrand wrote:

We hope you will answer the questions above:

First of all,  who is "We"?  Do you presume to represent the majority of =
list members?  I hardly think so as I am confidant in having expressed =
myself clearly enough for most having a rudimentary grasp of English to =
understand.  Or is that referring to Tinky-Winky, Dipsie, La-la, Poo and =
$=A3,   in which case it seems you are keeping good company.  I will,  =
however,  in a spirit of good sportsmanship,  indulge your questions,  =
even if they are an attempt to bait me.

By the way,  your e-mail arrived at  5:12 PM Pacific time,  which would =
be 3:12 AM in Sweden....you're losing sleep over this?

While you still thought the Hum was directed (towards you), did your Hum =

sound like a) (minus >>lacking directionality<<), b) or c)?

Nice try.  We can detect the directionality of sound,  which moves at a =
leisurely 1,116 feet per second,  because our brains can determine the =
time differential between the sound wave entering first one ear and then =
the other.  However,  with EMR travelling at 186,282 miles per second =
the time differential would be too small to detect and anyway,  the =
normal mechanism of hearing is not involved in the EM theory of the hum, =
 so even if an experimental beam were directed on a volunteer at a =
frequency capable of biological coupling,  there would be no sense of =
it's directionality. =20

Is, according to your opinion, a), b) or c) the Taos Hum?

You already know that a) is the answer to that.  The descriptions =
offered by the first observers that I heard of 6 years ago match my own =
perfectly,  and it was then that the term "Taos Hum" entered popular =
usage.  As I said,  there appear to be other hums,  but I am concerned =
with the taos kind as I believe there to be a real and present health =
hazard.  Since then there have been many fanciful accounts that do not =
fit with my experience or those who seriously investigated this,  and I =
don't know what to say about those.

How come that "random EM pollution" does not sound like white or pink=20
noise.

Because it is not white or pink noise,  that our ears can hear.  To a =
pan-spectrum receiver,  it would sound like white noise,  otherwise =
known as static.  But we are not hearing it.  We are having an auditory =
type hallucination caused by certain frequencies that have the =
characteristic of interacting with biological systems and the hum is a =
symptom of a greater effect perpetrated upon that organism.  And because =
the hum is only a symptom,  not everyone gets it.  Is this concept =
really so difficult?  And I have ventured it as a theory based on my =
experience combined with the findings of some excellent research,  the =
links to which have frequently been posted to this list.  I am not just =
making this up out of thin air,  and do not claim it to be fact,  only a =
suggestion of possibility.

Does this mean that you no longer believe that cell phones and their=20
transmitter grid causes your Hum?

I never believed this,  simply because I have had the hum since 1982,  =
long before cell phones.  That is not to say cell phones and all the =
additional microwaves in the environment are not harmful in other,  =
perhaps much more dangerous,  ways.

If ELF EMR has "extremely little energy loss", does this not mean that =
only=20
a small fraction of the energy transmitted by a few ELF transmitters =
must=20
be driving the world wide Hum? What mechanism do you propose for this=20
energy conversion and to what kind of energy is the ELF EMR energy loss=20
converted? (Obviously not converted to acoustic energy, the kind of =
energy=20
which could be heard and recorded by a microphone since:)

I'm not sure what your point is here,  but in general energy loss is =
expressed as heat.  Since it is mountains,  oceans,  forests,  that =
absorb most of the higher frequencies the conversion to heat is of =
minute proportions because of the enormous mass involved.  And if =
certain low frequencies interact on a cellular level in a process not =
involving heat (athermal),  then the energy required may be extremely =
small.=20

Since the alleged 'non-recordability' of the type a) Hum seems to imply=20
that the energy driving the Hum sensation is _not_ acoustic, what is =
then=20
the distinction between type a) Hum and type c) Hum?

You clever nit-picker.  Yes,  strictly speaking,  type a) then is in =
fact a kind of internally caused hum since there is not in fact a hum =
outside of the affected organism,  even though the energy driving the =
process is coming from OUTSIDE that organism,  whereas with the type c) =
hum the internally caused symptoms are entirely created WITHIN the =
affected organism,  requiring no external energy source other than =
perhaps some form of medication.  So you see,  there is still that very =
important difference.  With c) there is no general electopollution =
problem needing to be addressed,  but with a) there most definitely =
would be. And a)would affect everyone,  whether they get the superficial =
symptom of a hum or not;  while c) is purely an individual problem of =
minor consequence.  There is a steadily growing body of evidence linking =
CFS,  fibromyalgia,  insomnia, depression,  and a host of cancers to =
even small amounts of RF EMR.  (that means "radio frequency =
electromagnetic radiation",  to make the distinction from other sources =
of EM.) The problem with RF EMR is the very precise timing of the wave,  =
like a drumbeat,  completely unnatural,  and our bodies have not evolved =
a mechanism of defense in the presence of these fields.   It was Dr. =
Becker who first identified the effects of what he more precisely called =
"time varying fields",  compared to the steady fields of permanent =
magnets,  for instance,  which do not appear to be harmful except =
perhaps at huge field strengths. Radio energy extant in the natural =
environment is random,  without fixed frequencies,  and therefore =
harmless.  It is the fixed,  man-made frequencies that are the problem.  =
And we are awash in a sea of them 24/7 for the first time in our history =
on this planet,  at appreciable energy levels only for the last few =
decades....the jury is still out and I suggest we are in for a few =
surprises when the last word is in,  if there is ever such a thing!=20

-Alf Bangert

Thursday, September 13 2001 you wrote: 

>Local industrial noise of course could be recorded,  but doesn't explain a 
>loud hum on the Juneau Icefield for instance which most likely could not 
>be recorded by any audio equipment.

Are you saying that for example the Hum recordings by Richard Loose in the 
desert of NM are industrial noise? This is extremely odd in the light of 
your own observation:

>Underway that morning,  I chose a more attractive site a little further on 
>to cook some breakfast,  and became aware of a sort of hum,  not quite 
>like the usual.  About a quarter of a mile further on the source revealed 
>itself as a pumping station for that same pipeline.  I passed it and about 
>a mile beyond stopped once more,  turning off the engine and listening 
>very intently,  heard nothing.  So although the pumping stations do give 
>off acoustic VLF's,  they do not travel particularly far.

Richard Loose was definitely convinced that the Hum he could hear was 
reproduced by his recordings.

I have been present while Anders Heerfordt has made some of his excellent 
Hum recordings, at the same time as I have been hearing the Hum as usual. 
The recordings have been close enough to the Hum I hear.

Is your interpretation that Anders' recorded some unspecified industrial 
noise at a recording site which was more than ten miles from the nearest 
industry, an industrial noise which furthermore sounded exactly like the 
Hum I hear. I could certainly _not_ hear any industrial noise at the 
recording site and I can tell the difference between the Hum and noise 
pollution coming from a specific direction.

So, according to 'the scientific method' which lately has been discussed so 
intently on the Taoshum-L, the recordability of the Hum is 'a crucial 
experiment'. If you subscribe to the scientific method you cannot simply 
_deny_ the experience derived from a crucial experiment. You are required 
to repeat the experiment and to communicate any differing results, or else 
you are required not to express an opinion.

My point exactly!  Sound always has a direction,  the hum does not.  I =
also can always tell the difference.  And if the hum were an acoustic =
phenomenon,  why would it sound exactly the same in places thousands of =
miles apart,  near civilization,  and also hundreds of miles from =
anywhere in the Canadian Arctic?  Perhaps,  living in Sweden,  you =
cannot comprehend vast tracts of land with absolutely no human activity =
of any sort.  What would an acoustic hum be doing in places like that,  =
and furthermore,  at the same volume level as anywhere else!!! The only =
form of energy wave that can be that uniform over huge distances is ELF =
RF EMR.  This does not require rocket science.  It is just common sense. =
 Acoustic pressure waves diminish in amplitude rather quickly as they =
radiate from their source.  It is true that very low frequencies carry =
further,  but even there,  a noticeable reduction in volume is achieved =
by removing oneself some distance from the source.  You know,  for about =
the first 10 years that I had this curse,  I also thought it was =
acoustic.  Maybe you just haven't had it long enough to be forced to =
abandon that futile concept.  Here's an example:  I live about a km from =
the local community hall,  which from time to time hosts a dance.  =
During summer,  the bands play with doors open and I get,  at that =
distance,  only the bass which is rather annoying.  At those times I put =
on earmuff type hearing protectors and this cuts out the bass enough so =
I can sleep.  Now,  putting on the earmuffs when the only "sound" is the =
hum,  makes no difference at all.  The hum is not affected by hearing =
protection,  not even a little bit.  On the contrary,  if the hum were =
totally internally caused,  putting on earmuff hearing protection should =
do the opposite,  actually increasing the hum by masking outside noise.  =
But that doesn't happen either.  Putting on the earmuffs simply has zero =
effect on the hum.  It is not acoustic.  Any recordings that have been =
made are serendipitous likenesses caused by artifact,  industrial noise, =
 or perhaps even,  EM frequencies directly interacting with the =
microphone,  using the voice coil as an antenna. =20

So, according to 'the scientific method' which lately has been discussed =
so=20

_deny_ the experience derived from a crucial experiment. You are =

you are required not to express an opinion.=20

Alf, I think your idea merits testing. The other hypothesis consisent with
ubiquitous "hum" hearing is an endogenously generated sensation -- the "fill
in" hypothesis I posted a while ago.

To summarize: the idea, advanced by HAARP expert Marshall Smith
(www.brojon.com), is that the auditory system is filling in specific
frequencies corresponding to cochlear system perception frequencies have
been damaged by exposure to low-frequency sounds. One support for this
hypothesis is that fact (to be checked) that the phenomenon only shows up in
adults.

Can we develop some solid experimental protocols for testing these (and
other)hypotheses?

Two proposed simple tests to get us started thinking about this:

1. ELF hypothesis: feed various ELF frequencies into a sub-20 Hz transducer
and note any that are perceptible. Perceptible frequencies can then be
related to naturally occuring ELF frequencies as noted in
http://www-star.stanford.edu/~mfuelle/eicr.html to determine possible
causes.

2. Fill-in hypothesis: hum sufferers can get an audiogram and identify
frequencies matching the perceived hum. If frequencies exist at which the
subject does not hear the tone match the perceived hum, this hypothesis
would be strongly supported.

Please examine these test protocols and see if there are any logical
fallacies. Note that results from these preliminary tests, while highly
informative, would not result in a scientific theory, which would require a
full experimental design, including double-blind protocols, control for
random RF and sound effects by appropriate sheilding, neurological tests,
peer review, multiple independent testing, etc.

Correction to my previous post: testing should not be limited to under 20
Hz. Of special interest would be 50 and 60 Hz frequencies (RF, not audio),
since they are the strongest global ELF frequencies (see
http://www-star.stanford.edu/~mfuelle/eicr.html).

Also, the perceived frequency and the transmitted RF frequencies don't have
to match. In other words, if a hum sufferer perceives a sound when an 8 Hz
RF frequency is used, but perceives it at, say, 100 Hz (audio frequency),
this would be highly significant, since there may be unpredictable effects
due to the well-known nonlinear response of the cochlear and auditory
cortical systems and possible intermodulation effects.

Of course, if the perceived audio frequency happens to match the transmitted
RF frequency, this would also be significant and interesting, but not a
necessary condition.

Another test would be to transmit RF ELF frequencies corresponding to
perceived audio frequencies. (A double-blind protocol, of course, is
mandatory here.)

Previous statement:

1. ELF hypothesis: feed various ELF frequencies into a sub-20 Hz transducer
and note any that are perceptible. Perceptible frequencies can then be
related to naturally occuring ELF frequencies as noted in
http://www-star.stanford.edu/~mfuelle/eicr.html to determine possible
causes.

Wes and all others,

here is my contribution to testing for the hum, an easy method most of us should
be able to follow:

There is a  simple way of finding a hummer's perceived frequency.
I'm most interested in getting a number of individuals to doing this test in
order to get a clearer picture about the tonal range of the hum(s) heard.

Everyone who hears hum can do this test. All which is required is a soundcard,
earmuffs, earphones (from a discman) and a PC - preferably a quiet notebook.
I have posted the test procedure before but the feedback was nil, so I am trying
this again:
first, you need software, please download it and install it on your PC:

http://www.powerup.com.au/~pfreihof/hum/sinewave.zip (185 kByte)
http://www.powerup.com.au/~pfreihof/hum/sweepgen.exe (374 kByte)

the Sweepgen.exe is the unzipped version of the Sinewave.zip.

What you need:
a high quality battery driven sine wave generator - alternatively a battery
powered laptop PC with a sound card running a software implemented sine wave
generator, a reasonably good quality set of head(ear) phones, a quiet (and I
mean
as quiet as possible) listening environment and finally of course THE HUM!
Note: to cut out any unwanted environmental noise use earmuffs, covering your
ears and earphones.

Tune the sinewave generator to a frequency range of 40...100 Hz and let it sweep

through this range within 20 seconds or so. Just get the hang of the frequency
generator by turning its dials, volume control etc. Then try to decrease the
output volume to the point where you can hardly hear the pure sinusoidal tones.
You'll notice that the threshold of hearing the tones is lower at the higher end

(100 Hz in this example) - this is because the sensitivity of the ear rolls off
by going low in frequency. As you sweep through the lower end of your hearing
range, compare the tones with the hum frequency. This way you should be able to
roughly tell if the generated tones are above or below the hum frequency. Once
this is established, narrow the sweep range from 40...100 Hz to a range with
just
covers the hum frequency (you should be able to narrow it down to a few Hz).
Make sure the volume for this narrow range is just above the threshold of
hearing. Now you decrease the sweeping speed down to about 40 seconds or so. The

output of the tone generator now slowly increases the frequency to the dialed
upper frequency and then loops back and starts again at the lower frequency,
continuing the cycle. If the sweep window covers the hum frequency you'll notice

some interference in the form of beating. It's a bit like tuning a string
instrument. The closer the tones get to the hum frequency the slower the
beating.
This works for both higher and lower end. So f.e. if your hum were at 71.3 Hz
you'd be able to count the same number of beats per minute at 69.3 Hz as at 73.3

Hz. With a bit of practice you'll be able to very accurately determine the
frequency at which you perceive the hum.
Please feel free to ask questions.
BTW there are some pitfalls in every individual setup of the experiment which
need careful attention.

I look forward to receive your feed back.
cheers, Peter.

Stefan,

I am not sure what Rich is up to.
But Anders' way of "recording hum" as far as he let me understand it so
far, is flawed.

All recordings of any signals (like hum, if it were an acoustic signal)
contain unwanted noise.

In order to distinguish between a signal (i.e hum) and artificial noise
(generated by the recording equipment), one has to compare the signal
with the adjoining noise.
This can only be achieved by a flat response (equal sensitivity) of the
recording equipment in the frequency range of interest. If any band pass
filtering is applied then these filters need to have the corner
frequencies set at several octaves apart.
If you do not follow this rule then you generate pink noise which can
easily be mistaken for the hum, especially if the pink noise band is
centered around the perceived hum frequency. The center of the pink
noise band is filter dependent and can easily be shifted up and down.
One only has to play with the filters a bit until he/she will hear a
sound which matches the hum closely.
This is artificially made hum, or a fake - which as you know from my
earlier posting can be achieved much easier.
In other words, you create hum in your recordings by applying narrow
bandpass filtering. This is Anders' method as he explained it to me
earlier.
Neither Anders nor yourself have to date given me the frequency of your
perceived hum although this can easily be determined by using a method I
repeatedly posted a few hours ago.

As I said before, one has to be able to compare the recorded sound level
@ the perceived hum frequency with adjoining sound levels. And only if
there is a significantly elevated signal strength at the perceived hum
frequency, then this is a positive result.

cheers, Peter.

I've noticed a pervasive logical fallacy in many posts on this list: a
tendency to overgeneralize, aggregating a wide variety of reported
sensations, often with different descriptions, under a single rubric known
as "the hum" or worse, "the Taos hum," as if some mysterious powerful sound
or RF signal was being emitted from Taos, New Mexico and travelling all
around the world. The assumption here, which is unsupported by any evidence
(AFAIK), is that these various reports are somehow connected by some
undefined massive global energy source or else that there are local sources,
all with the same parameters, despite any evidence of a common energy
source. (However, if Alf's global ELF hypothesis is confirmed, such
aggregation may be supported in certain cases. BTW, we should also consider
ULF signals, which are below 3 Hz and thus travel globally more easily and
tend to be correlated with earthquakes and mood.)

A correlary of this fallacy is the assumption, implicit in many posts, that
there is only one possible explanation: _________ (insert pet speculation
here) for all of these various reported sensations. For example, tinnitus
can have multiple causes, ranging from inner-ear infection to zinc
deficiency. There's no logical reason why "the hum," whatever that means,
has a single cause. In addition, many conditions in the body can result from
synergy between multiple causes. For example, a specific "hum" sensation
might result from a combination of, say, high stress levels, mild infection,
and electrical hypersensitivity induced by years of exposure to EMF fields.

Sorting through all of these causes under for a wide variety of
environmental conditions and personal differences makes this a challenging
detective game. I would be surprised if there turn out to be simple
explanations.

I am not really following the discussion here, but I saw Peter's message on
recording pitfalls, and I think a short comment is called for.

There are many pitfalls in the recording of hums.

One of them is the artificial hum generated, not by filtering, but by the
electronic noise in amplifiers and detectors.
One method, but not the only one, of discerning between artificial noise
generated by the amplifiers and environmental noise picked up by the detectors,
is frequency analysis (typically by Fourier transformation). It is good practice
to record using flat frequency response detectors, amplifiers and recorders, and
I have indeed done so, with so. In the cases where I have used geophones, one
could argue that the geophones do not have as flat a frequency response as
piezoelectric tranducers. There has been a trade off here, the geophones have a
better signal/noise ratio and a poorer frequency response.

So my recordings have been done with flat frequency responses typically from 10
to 100 Hz. Frequency analysis shows the majority of the hum is from the
environment, not generated as electronic noise inside the equipment.

But whether the recordings are "identical" to the hum perceived at the location,
is an entirely different question, which is open to discussion.

Regards, Anders

>Stefan wrote:
>.........................
>I suppose you have followed the debate I have recently had with Peter
>Freihofner and Alf Bangert regarding the recordability of the Hum.
>
>Both of them have flatly denied that the Hum recordings performed by
>Rich
>Loose and Anders Heerfordt -- both qualified engineers -- are in fact
>recordings of the Hum.
>.........................
>
>Stefan,
>
>I am not sure what Rich is up to.
>But Anders' way of "recording hum" as far as he let me understand it so
>far, is flawed.
>
>All recordings of any signals (like hum, if it were an acoustic signal)
>contain unwanted noise.
>
>In order to distinguish between a signal (i.e hum) and artificial noise
>(generated by the recording equipment), one has to compare the signal
>with the adjoining noise.
>This can only be achieved by a flat response (equal sensitivity) of the
>recording equipment in the frequency range of interest. If any band pass
>filtering is applied then these filters need to have the corner
>frequencies set at several octaves apart.
>If you do not follow this rule then you generate pink noise which can
>easily be mistaken for the hum, especially if the pink noise band is
>centered around the perceived hum frequency. The center of the pink
>noise band is filter dependent and can easily be shifted up and down.
>One only has to play with the filters a bit until he/she will hear a
>sound which matches the hum closely.
>This is artificially made hum, or a fake - which as you know from my
>earlier posting can be achieved much easier.
>In other words, you create hum in your recordings by applying narrow
>bandpass filtering. This is Anders' method as he explained it to me
>earlier.
>Neither Anders nor yourself have to date given me the frequency of your
>perceived hum although this can easily be determined by using a method I
>repeatedly posted a few hours ago.
>
>As I said before, one has to be able to compare the recorded sound level
>@ the perceived hum frequency with adjoining sound levels. And only if
>there is a significantly elevated signal strength at the perceived hum
>frequency, then this is a positive result.
>
>cheers, Peter.
>

> Hi Cathy, I'm curious, are you sure the hum has really changed or are you
> focusing more on it, and have finally started to hear the top, or higher
> tone notes?? I'm very interrested in the tone aspect, I dont hear it as a
> hum. I hear it as 2 distinct, seperate tones, not a hum. Rick


Hi Rick,

Well, I've been hearing this since the mid 70's and have pretty much stopped
obsessing on it.  The "oldest" of the noices I hear is similar to listening
to the engine of a deisel train idling a couple hundred yards down the
track.  Some times closer, some times further away.  This is the sound that
I'm almost never without and it is not directional.  However, in the last
month, there have been periods of around 1 hour usually but not always
around 9pm to 10pm pacific time that it's not there.  At this point, I
notice it when it's not there rather than when it is.  This is the sound
that I have described in the past as a "hum", maybe roar would be better.

As for the other two tones, it is possible that I just never searched for
them.  It is true that since joining this list I have taken the time to
actually "listen" to the tones.  The two higher pitched tones are familiar
and as you describe, separate.  They remind me of the sort of sound you
might hear from say a 12v tranformer plugged into your wall or the whine a
copy machine makes when warming up.  The thing is that I have been riding my
horse out into the wilderness and listening.  There are no 12v tranformers
plugged in out there, so that's not what I'm hearing.  I would describe them
as "thin" and high pitched.  Thin is the only word I can think of, don't
know if you understand.  These sounds tend to be more directional, louder
when facing one direction or another.  While I have noticed these sounds in
the past, they have been fleeting, where as now, they are more constant.

Hope this helps, Cathy

>

<

Generate some wav files, and burn these onto a CDROM, to be played on a
CD-player, for example.
A CD player has a much higher fidelity and signal/noise ratio than the average
soundcard.

When you play low level low frequency tones on a Soundblaster 16, there is for
example sufficient higher frequency noise in the output signal to make the
signal unsuitable for determination of auditory threshold without special
filtering. Therefore you sometimes either need a high quality soundcard, or a
CDROM.

Or you would make a wav-file to test the program, to see  how precisely the
frequency in the dialogbox matches the frequency of the output..

How do you make a wav-file with the nifty little program??

Hi Rick,

if you have already unzipped the first file and used the prog then don't worry
about the second one - it's just the same prog in an unzipped file.

Now to your observations of the added tower platform
It is very common to utilize high structures for mounting antennas and dishes.
So what you observed is probably the mounting of another antenna on an already
existing antenna - piggybacking isn't this how it's called?

That the towers were silent for this kind of work to be performed doesn't
surprise me. That you did not hear your tones at this time is either a very very
big coincidence or the towers are truly the source for your tone sensations.

cheers, Peter.

Anders,

you could have asked me something easier...
I don't know how to directly convert the output of this prog to a wav file.
But what I did very successfully on my notebook (which has a Yamaha sound processor
integrated) was feeding back the output of the sound card to its input.
Then I used the Win98 accessory prog "sound recorder" to record the sound.
This gives me a resulting S/N of almost 90 dB on my system.
If you record your tones at the greatest possible volume @ a recording noise floor
of -90 dB and play the recorded wavs back at low SPLs (which you do for hearing
threshold tests anyway) then you won't be able to hear any noise, just the clean
pure recorded signals.
Does this help?

Now to the frequency accuracy of the nifty little sine generator.
I've compared a 50 Hz generated sine wave with the mains 50 Hz and found it spot on
(at least to 0.1% accurate).
Also, from memory I think it was Alf Bangert who compared the frequency accuracy to
a commercial electronic tuning fork and he also found it spot on @ several hundred
Hz.

The only thing to keep in mind is that you MUST NOT use the up and down arrows on
the GUI because due to a software bug, this can lead to a significant discrepancy
between the indicated frequency and the actual output frequency - the frequ.
accuracy goes bye bye.

Till then, have a great time.
cheers, Peter.

This is (and has been) the case. Some of the first "real-world" tests of 
re-encoding EMI/EMF radiation were done way back in the 60s (possibly 
earlier) under the guise of "TEMPEST" monitoring. This enabled a person 
to pickup field radiation from electronic devices from miles away and 
recreate that data on a computer. This opened a whole new realm of 
options, as humans like everything else emit a certain degree of EMI/EMF 
radiation. This technology was FULLY classified until 1999 when it was 
partly released. Some people have come very far on this path but, Van 
Eck would be the "leader" in home-made TEMPEST devices.

But all that is only on the gathering end of the scope .. on the 
flipside you have the whole aspect of generating EMI/EMF radiation, in 
sync with something like a human brain, that would be picked up from a 
distance and processed.

Hope all is well bob, your posts always envoke thought!

John

I began hearing the hum two years ago when we moved to our new house, =
which is about 4 miles from the Pacific Ocean in Washington. There is =
not much of anything around here, and I was enjoying the silence of our =
rural home.  I began to notice that I was hearing a distant hum when =
everything else was quiet-no vehicles, no appliances running-nothing.  I =
thought that it must be some nearby lumber mill or something.  It =
defnitely sounds like low-pitched machinery.  I discovered quite by =
accident that many others all over the world are hearing the same type =
of noise.  I even thought that it might be the transformer in our back =
yard, but that was eliminated as a source when we had a power outage of =
everything within about 30 miles, and I could still hear it.  It was =
very loud last night(10-10/11-2001), and today while I was outside, I =
could hear it very loudly down the hill behind our house.  I never heard =
it anywhere I lived before.  Those of us that hear it may not know what =
it is, but we do know that we hear it.  Last night while I was listening =
to it, it was punctuated by two distant thumps, which were probably =
sonic booms over the ocean.  This was at approximately 1:50 AM PDT.  =
Then, at about 2:15 am, there was another louder thump, which rattled =
windows and shook the bedroom door.  I had to go and check the news to =
make sure there weren't any more attacks occuring.  This probably isn't =
related, just thought I would mention it.

Greg Senderhauf

Dear greg and laura, I just read your letter.Welcome to this Taos web. Most 
of us are hearing or feeling something, around the world. I live north of 
Seattle and have heard these noises for about 2 years.I call it "Tones" 
because I hear the same 2 types of notes, like musical notes, one is a high 
note and the other one is a lower tone. There is a major naval 
communications site up here which is the cause of these Tones which I 
hear.It is near the mountains and the Towers can plainly be seen.They 
broadcast VLF frequencies to communicate.These frequencies travel through 
the ground to submarines around the globe, maybe only in the Pacific, I'm 
not sure.Thats what you and I are hearing. The distance and power 
requirements for this type of technology is incredable!!I dont have any 
other problems or symptoms, but this site is very active in a non-invasive 
way. All I hear is the same 2 tones, day and night. Sometimes it quits for 
awhile, overnight or part of the day.These tones are a direct result of 
these towers at this site, there isnt anything we can do about it, its the 
technology being used. There are several other similar sites throughout the 
globe. This is not a hum, because its 2 different tones.If I concentrate on 
the lower tone only, then it seems like it is a hum, but when I focus on 
both tones, the higher tone comes into the picture and the noise is no 
longer just a hum, but "Tones" instead.I think its very important for me to 
continue to distinguish these factors whenever I write about these towers up 
here, so as to differentiate between what I am hearing, compared to the rest 
of the world and writers who contribute here.What you are hearing is the

thought that it must be some nearby lumber mill or something.  It =
defnitely sounds like low-pitched machinery.  I discovered quite by =
accident that many others all over the world are hearing the same type =
of noise.  I even thought that it might be the transformer in our back =
yard, but that was eliminated as a source when we had a power outage of =

very loud last night(10-10/11-2001), and today while I was outside, I =

it is, but we do know that we hear it.  Last night while I was listening =
